Corsica, Sardinia and Liguria rebel unsuccessfully against Rome.
The Qin general Huan Yi wins a major victory over the Zhao general Hu Zhe in the Battle of Pingyang, and captures Pingyang and Wucheng.
The city of Pleuron is destroyed by Demetrius II of Macedon.
The Zhao general Li Mu defeats the Qin army, led by Huan Yi, in the Battle of Fei.
The Zhao general Li Mu defeats the Qin army in the Battle of Fanwu.

The king of Qin, Ying Zheng, invites Prince Han Fei, a legalist philosopher and member of the Han royal family, to the Qin court. However, at the instigation of Li Si, he then has him imprisoned and executed as a threat to the state.
The Romans send envoys to Massilia (modern Marseille, France) to negotiate with the Carthaginian general Hamilcar Barca who is based there.
The state of Han is conquered by the state of Qin.
Aratus of Sicyon brings Argos into the Achaean League and then helps liberate Athens. This brings Aratus into conflict with Sparta.
Concerned at Rome's expansion, Antigonus III pursues a policy of befriending the Illyrians, even though the Greeks in the region support Rome in quelling the Illyrian pirates.
The Illyrian tribe of the Ardiaei is subdued by the Romans.

Hasdrubal makes immediate policy changes, emphasizing the use of diplomatic rather than military methods for expanding Carthaginian Hispania and dealing with Rome. He founds Carthago Nova or New Carthage (modern Cartagena) as his capital city.
The State of Qin, its armies led by Wang Jian, completes the conquest of the State of Zhao.
Gaius Flaminius becomes Rome's first governor of Sicily.
The Qin generals Wang Jian, Li Xin and Wang Ben invade the State of Yan in vengeance for an assassination attempt against the king of Qin, Ying Zheng, that had been organized by Crown Prince Dan.
That same year, ex-Han nobility launched a failed rebellion against the Qin Forces. But in the end they were crushed.

The Greek merchants of Massilia, frightened by Carthaginian successes in Spain (including their exploitation of the Spanish silver mines), appeal to Rome. Rome makes an alliance with the independent Spanish port city of Saguntum south of the Ebro River.

The Qin generals Wang Jian, Li Xin and Wang Ben conquer western Yan and its capital Ji. To secure peace, king Xi of Yan executes his son Crown Prince Dan, who is wanted for the attempted assassination of the king of Qin, Ying Zheng.
The state of Qin, its armies led by Wang Ben, conquers the state of Wei.
Qin begins the invasion of Chu. Initially, the Qin generals Li Xin and Meng Tian capture several cities and defeat the Chu army.
Taking command of the Qin war effort, Wang Jian twice defeats Xiang Yan and captures Fuchu, the king of Chu, as well as the Chu capital Chen and the city of Pingyu.
King Diodotus II of Bactria is killed by a usurper, Euthydemus I, founder of the Greco-Bactrian Euthydemid dynasty.
The Qin generals Wang Ben and Li Xin conquer Liaodong, thereby completing the subjugation of Yan.
Wang Ben conquers Dai, thereby completing the subjugation of Zhao.
Gaius Flaminius builds a second race track for Rome, the Circus Flaminius.
King Cleomenes III of Sparta, who is in exile in Egypt, is imprisoned by Ptolemy IV on a charge of conspiracy.
A bronze statue called Gallic Chieftain killing his wife and himself is made. A Roman copy after the original statue is today preserved at Museo Nazionale Romano in Rome.
Demetrius seeks refuge with Philip V of Macedon, who is very resentful of the Roman interference. Rome occupies Demetrius' chief fortresses, Pharos and Dimillos.
Qin Shi Huang begins a system of tree-lined roads to interconnect all parts of China, and begins to join regional walls to form the beginnings of the Great Wall (Wan li chang cheng).
Qin Shi Huang orders his generals to capture present-day Guangdong and Guangxi.
The former King of Sparta, Cleomenes III, escapes from his Egyptian prison and, after failing to raise a revolt in Alexandria, takes his own life.
Carthaginians defeat the Romans at Lake Trasimene; at the Trebia River and at the Ticinus River
Hannibal advances to the Arno River and then outmanoeuvres the army of Gaius Flaminius at Arretium and reaches Faesulae (modern Fiesole) and Perugia.
Philip V of Macedon, continuing his war with the Aetolian League lays siege to Phthiotic Thebes, captures it and sells the inhabitants into slavery.
Second Punic War: Commanded by Hannibal, the Carthaginians ambushed a Roman army at the Battle of Lake Trasimene, capturing or killing 25,000 men.
After the defeat at Cannae, Roman general, Marcus Claudius Marcellus, commands the remnants of the Roman army at Canusium and saves the city of Nola and southern Campania from occupation by Hannibal.
Following Hannibal's victory, many regions begin to defect from Rome, while others are conquered by Hannibal's forces. In Apulia, Lucania, Samnium and in Bruttium, Hannibal finds many supporters.
The Carthaginian general, Hannibal, moves his forces southward through Italy and seizes the large army supply depot at Cannae on the Aufidus River.
Emperor Qin Shi Huang orders the construction of his mausoleum to begin(source?), including the famous Terracotta Army.
Hannibal's forces occupy the cities of Heraclea and Thurii. However, Hannibal is unable to prevent the Romans from besieging Capua.
The Roman general, Marcus Claudius Marcellus, again repulses an attack by Hannibal on the city of Nola.
Carthage persuades Syracuse to revolt against Rome and ally itself with Carthage instead.
Qin Shi Huang orders general Ren Xiao (任囂), commanding 200,000 troops, to conquer the kingdoms in present-day northern Vietnam.
Roman legions led by Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus defeat Hanno's Carthaginian forces in a battle near Beneventum, thus denying Hannibal much needed reinforcements.
Archimedes's war machines repel the Roman army that is invading Syracuse.
Casilinum and Arpi are recovered by the Romans from Hannibal.
Emperor Qin Shi Huang and Prime Minister Li Si order all Confucian writings destroyed in the burning of books and burying of scholars.
Antiochus III leaves for a campaign in Asia, where he will reach as far as India and mostly manage to recover the areas conquered earlier by Alexander the Great.
Tylis is destroyed by the Thracians.
Hannibal marches northwards on the city of Rome in a belated and unsuccessful effort to capture the city.
With the capture of Syracuse, the Romans are able to pacify all of Sicily.

Qin Er Shi becomes Emperor of the Qin dynasty of China. His advisors Zhao Gao and Prime Minister Li Si forge a decree by the late Emperor Qin Shi Huang that orders the execution of Qin Er Shi's elder brother Fusu and Fusu's ally, the general Meng Tian.
The Terracotta Army in the mausoleum of Emperor Shihuangdi, Lintong, Shaanxi, is made (Qin dynasty).
The famine and inflation facing Rome is eased with the pacification, by the Romans, of Sicily.
Jiao, Lord of Wey is deposed by Emperor Qin Er Shi, marking the end of the state of Wei
The Battle of Canusium is fought between Hannibal's Carthaginian army and a Roman force led by Marcus Claudius Marcellus. The battle is indecisive.
The Qin general Zhang Han defeats an invasion of Guanzhong by the rebel general Zhou Wen.
Hannibal destroys a Roman force at the Battle of Petelia.
Qin Prime Minister Li Si is executed by Qin Er Shi, having been conspired against by the eunuch Zhao Gao, who replaces him as Prime Minister.
Zhang Han seizes the Zhao capital Handan and besieges its king Zhao Xie in Julu.

Emperor Qin Er Shi of the Qin dynasty is assassinated by Prime Minister Zhao Gao. He is replaced by his nephew Ziying, who in turn assassinates Zhao Gao. Ziying takes power as the king of Qin rather than as emperor.
The Chu rebel Xiang Yu defeats the Qin general Zhang Han in the Battle of Julu and becomes the leader of the rebellion against the Qin dynasty.
Xiang Yu defeats Zhang Han in the Battle of the Yushui River. Zhang Han then surrenders to Xiang Yu.
The city of Italica (northwest of modern Seville, Spain) is founded by Scipio as a place to settle for the Roman soldiers wounded in the Battle of Ilipa.

The war between Macedonia and Rome drags on with no decisive advantage on either side. Rome's interest lies not in conquest, but in keeping Macedon, the Greek city-states and Greek political leagues continually divided and non-threatening.
Xiang Yu appoints Huai II of Chu as Emperor Yi of China, but he has him assassinated later in the year.
Han Xin captures Feiqiu, the last holdout of Zhang Han, thus completing the Han conquest of the Three Qins. Zhang Han commits suicide.
Han Xin defeats Wei Bao and conquers the kingdom of Wei.
The native Egyptian population rises in rebellion against their Greek rulers. The revolt spreads to Upper Egypt.
Han Xin completes the conquest of Zhao and receives the surrender of Yan. He captures the Zhao capital of Handan and defeats Chu relief forces sent by Xiang Yu.
Han Xin invades the State of Qi, defeats Qi's armies, captures their capital Linzi and crushes a coalition army of Chu and Qi forces under Long Ju in the Battle of the Wei River.
Han Xin completes the conquest of Qi, and Liu Bang appoints him as its king.
Hasdrubal Gisco persuades the Carthaginians to raise a new army and to send for Hannibal to return home from Italy. Hannibal finally leaves Italy and returns to Carthage.
Masinissa becomes king of both the Massyli and the Massaesyli tribes in Numidia and remains a loyal ally to the Romans.
During this period of confusion and change amongst Egypt’s leadership, armies under the Seleucid king, Antiochus III, make serious inroads into the Egyptian territories in Coele-Syria.
Rebel leader Liu Bang declared himself Emperor Gaozu of Han after overthrowing the Qin dynasty, the first imperial dynasty of China.
The Egyptian regent and chief minister, Sosibius, retires and Agathocles, another member of the ruling clique, becomes Ptolemy V's guardian.
The construction of the new Chinese capital Chang'an begins.
In Rome, according to the Roman historian Livy, land is distributed to veterans of the Second Punic War. This is the first documented instance of a practice that later becomes commonplace.

King Xin of Han, in alliance with Modu Chanyu of the Xiongnu, launches a rebellion against the Han dynasty in the Taiyuan Commandery. He is defeated by Emperor Gaozu of Han and his generals, who chase Xin of Han into Xiongnu territory.
Philip V of Macedon captures Samos and the Egyptian fleet stationed there. He then besieges Chios to the north.
The Han emperor Gaozu is defeated by the Xiongnu, led by Modu Chanyu, in the Battle of Baideng.
The construction of the Wei-Yang Palace in the Han dynasty capital (Chang'an) begins.
Ancient Egyptian Pharaoh Ankhwennefer succeeds Horwennefer in Upper Egypt, Egypt.
Scipio Africanus becomes censor and princeps Senatus (the titular head of the Roman Senate).
Antiochus III occupies parts of the kingdom of Pergamum and a number of Greek cities in Anatolia.
Chen Xi begins a rebellion against the Han dynasty in the Dai region of the northern frontier.
The Egyptian King, Ptolemy V, fights rebels in the Nile Delta, exhibiting great cruelty toward those of their leaders who capitulate.
Emperor Gaozu of Han and his generals, including Cao Shen and Zhou Bo, defeat the rebellion of Chen Xi.
The Insubres, Gauls of the Po Valley, believed by the Romans to have been incited to revolt by Carthage, are finally defeated.
The first triumphal arch built in Rome.
Chang'an, the capital of China, is thought to become the largest city in the world at this time, taking over from Pataliputra, the capital of the Mauryan empire.
Facing the suspicion of Emperor Gaozu of Han, Lu Wan, the king of the State of Yan, flees north of the Great Wall of China.
Tensions between Antiochus III and Rome increase when Hannibal is given refuge by Antiochus III at Ephesus and becomes his adviser.
Philip V of Macedon, along with Rhodes, Pergamum, and the Achaean League, join Rome against Antiochus III.
The Wiman Joseon kingdom of northern Korea (Choson) is founded by the Chinese Han dynasty general Wiman.

With his peace agreement with the Egyptians in place, Antiochus III now turns his attention to the West. He is encouraged to challenge Rome's protection of the Greeks by his advisor, the former Carthaginian general Hannibal.
Carneades of Cyrene moves to Athens to found the third or new Academy.

Flamininus is sent to negotiate with Antiochus III and warns him not to interfere with the Greek states. Antiochus does not accept that Flamininus has the authority to speak for the Greeks and promises to leave Greece alone only if the Romans do the same.
The first porticos were built in Rome.

Philopoemen's plans for capturing Sparta itself are put on hold at the request of the Roman envoy Flaminius after his arrival in Greece. In return, Nabis decides, for the moment, to accept the status quo.
Cisalpine Gaul becomes a Roman province.
Emperor Hui of Han lifts the ban on Confucian writings ordered in 213 BC.
The Roman calendar, which is four months ahead of the seasons, is adjusted (by Lex Acilia de intercalando).

As Philip V of Macedon has aided Rome against her enemies on the Greek peninsula, his tribute to Rome is remitted and his son, Demetrius, is restored to him after being held hostage in Rome for a number of years.
One of the main highways in Roman Italy, the Via Appia, is extended to Benevento and Venosa.
Subsequently, the naval Battle of Myonessus is fought between a Seleucid fleet and a Roman fleet with the help of Rhodian ships. The Romans and their allies are victorious.
The territory of Artsakh first became known for being inhabited by Armenians-notably within the city of Tigranakert, one of four cities named after Tigranes the Great in the ancient Armenian empire.
Hannibal flees via Crete to the court of King Prusias I of Bithynia who is engaged in warfare with Rome's ally, King Eumenes II of Pergamum.
The continuing quarrels among the Greek cities and leagues increases the conviction in Rome that there will be no peace in Greece until Rome takes full control.

The Seleucid king, Antiochus III, attempts to collect tribute from a temple near Susa, Persia, where he was killed. He is succeeded by his son, Seleucus IV, who inherits an empire consisting of Syria, Mesopotamia, Babylonia, western Iran.
The first burial at the famous archaeological site of Mawangdui is made during the Western Han dynasty of China.
Pushyamitra Shunga assassinates the Mauryan emperor Brhadrata, which brings an end to that dynasty, after which he founds the Shunga dynasty.
The civil war between the northern and southern areas of Egypt ends with the arrest of Ankmachis by the Ptolemaic general Conanus.

The oldest known basilica, the Basilica Porcia, is completed in Rome by Cato the Elder during the time he is censor. The building is used by the Romans for transacting business and disposing of legal matters.
The town of Pisaurum is established by the Romans as a colony in the territory of the Picentes, a tribe living in the Marche on the Adriatic.

With concerns rising in Rome over whether Philip V of Macedon is preparing for a new war with the Romans, Appius Claudius Pulcher is sent at the head of an embassy into Macedonia and Greece to observe Philip's activities.
Roman colonies are established at Mutina (later Modena), Pisa and Parma in northern and central Italy.
Nanyue's emperor Zhao Tuo attacks the other vassal kingdoms of Minyue, Western Ou and Luo and secures their submission. He also attacks the state of Changsha.
Rome founds a colony at Aquileia, on the narrow strip of land between the mountains and the lagoons, as a frontier fortress to check the advance of the Illyrians.

After three years of intriguing against his younger brother Demetrius, including accusing him of coveting the succession to the Macedonian throne and being allied to Rome, Perseus persuades his father King Philip V of Macedon to have Demetrius executed.
Rome completes its subjugation of all of Italy with the defeat of the Ligurians in a battle near modern Genoa. Rome deports 40,000 Ligurians to other areas of the Republic.
The Pons Aemilius is completed across the Tiber River in Rome. It is regarded as the world's first stone bridge.
Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus goes to Hispania as Roman governor to deal with uprisings there.
After two military campaigns, the Romans finally subdue the Illyrian tribe of the Histri.
Luni in northern Italy is founded by the Romans with the name Luna at the mouth of the Magra River.
The Roman general, Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus, subdues Sardinia, enslaving some of the population.
Antiochus manages to oust Heliodorus and takes advantage of Demetrius' captivity in Rome to seize the throne for himself under the name Antiochus IV Epiphanes.
The first street pavements were laid in Rome.
Antiochus IV pays the remainder of the war indemnity that has been imposed by the Romans on Antiochus III in the Treaty of Apamea (188 BC).

Eumenes II of Pergamum travels to Rome to warn the Roman Senate of the danger from Perseus of Macedon. On his return from Rome, Eumenes II is nearly killed at Delphi and Perseus is suspected of being the instigator.
Boiotian League dissolved by the Romans.
Epirus joins Macedonia in the latter's fight against Rome. However, the leagues of southern Greece remain neutral.
In Thessaly, King Perseus of Macedon repulses a Roman army which is commanded by Aulus Hostilius Mancinus. Meanwhile, the Thracian city of Abdera is sacked by Roman and Pergamese troops.
Jason removes Menelaus as High Priest in Jerusalem, which Antiochus IV regards as an affront to his majesty.
The joint rulers of Egypt, Ptolemy VI, Ptolemy VIII Euergetes II and their sister Cleopatra II send a renewed request to Rome for aid.
King Antiochus IV Epiphanes, believing Judea to be in revolt, returns there after the failure of his Egyptian campaign.
Private documents collected by the Romans when they capture Perseus of Macedon incriminate political leaders of the Achaean League. Many influential Greeks are deported to Rome.

The Parthians capture the key central Asian city of Herat. This victory effectively chokes off the movement of trade along the Silk Road to China and means that the Hellenic kingdom of Bactria is doomed.
The Roman playwright Terence's Andria (The Girl from Andros) is first performed.
The Roman playwright Terence's play Hecyra (The Mother-in-Law) is first performed.
Rhodes signs a treaty with Rome and becomes its ally.
The Egyptian King Ptolemy VI Philometor is expelled from Alexandria by his brother Ptolemy VIII Euergetes and flees to Rome to seek support.
The Roman playwright Terence's play Heauton Timorumenos ("The Self-Tormentor") is first performed.
Envoys of Judas Maccabeus conclude a treaty of friendship with the Roman Senate.
The Roman playwright Terence's plays Eunuchus (The Eunuch) and Phormio are first performed.
A Painted banner, from the tomb of the wife of the Marquis of Dai, of the Han dynasty, in Mawangdui, Changsha, Hunan, is made. It is nowadays preserved at the Historical museum in Beijing.

The king of Bactria, Eucratides I, is considered to have killed Apollodotus I, an Indo-Greek king who rules the western and southern parts of the Indo-Greek kingdom, when he invades the western territories of that kingdom.

After his victory, Attalus II insists on heavy reparations from Prusias II. In response, Prusias II sends his son Nicomedes to Rome to ask the Romans' help in reducing the amount of these reparations.
The Lusitanians harry the inhabitants of the Roman provinces in Hispania. At the same time, the Celtiberians of Numantia on the Douro revolt against their Roman occupation.

The Rebellion of the Seven States against the Han dynasty fails and Emperor Jing of Han further consolidates his power at the expense of the regional, semi-autonomous kings governing the eastern portion of the empire.
Substantial parts of the city of Sikyon are destroyed by an earthquake.
Agnimitra succeeds his father Pushyamitra Shunga as emperor of the Shunga dynasty.
Roman forces help the thriving Greek commercial port of Massilia combat raids from the Celts from Cisalpine Gaul.
The enlargement of the Great Stupa of Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh, India begins, taking about 100 years.
The making of the statue Hellenistic Ruler begins and is finished ten years later. It is now kept at the Museo Nazionale Romano in Rome.
The new king of the Seleucid Empire, Alexander Balas, marries Cleopatra Thea, a daughter of Ptolemy VI Philometor of Egypt.
Andriscus, the last king of Macedon, ascends to the throne.
The Third Punic War begins. The Romans land an army in Africa to begin the Battle of Carthage.
With Roman help, Nicomedes II overthrows his father Prusias II as king of Bithynia.
In Lusitania, Hispania, the Celtic king Viriathus, rallies Lusitanian resistance to Rome.
Achaean War: The Romans conquer the Achaean League and southern Greece becomes a Roman province.
Carthage falls to Roman forces under Scipio Aemilianus and the city is completely destroyed. End of the Third Punic War.
Roman armies destroy Carthage and Corinth.
Ptolemy VII becomes king of Egypt briefly, then is assassinated by Ptolemy VIII the following year.
Diodotus Tryphon seizes the throne of the Seleucid Empire.
Demetrius II of Syria made prisoner of Mithridates, king of the Parthians. Antiochus VII Sidetes becomes king of the Seleucid Empire in his absence.
Emperor Wu of Han ("Martial Emperor") starts to rule the Han dynasty.
The Seleucid garrison negotiates the surrender of Jerusalem. Simon Maccabaeus assumes control of the city. He becomes prince (ruler) of Judea until 135 BC.
Scipio Aemilianus leads a group of Roman ambassadors to Alexandria, where they meet with King Ptolemy VIII.
The Lusitanian War ends when the rebellion collapses after the assassination of Viriathus by a Roman agent.
Phraates II becomes emperor of Parthia.
Valencia in Spain is founded as a Roman colony.
Confucianism is adopted as the state religion in China by Emperor Wu.
The Romans hand Gaius Hostilius Mancinus over to the Numantians in order to repudiate his peace treaty with them.
A Han military campaign against the Dian Kingdom establishes a military commandery in the Yunnan region.
Emperor Wu makes Zou Chou the king of Minyue, but Zou Yushan carves out two thirds of Minyue as the state of Dongyue, which Wu then recognizes.

Minyue attacks Nanyue, which are both vassal states of the Han dynasty. The Han send two armies against Minyue under Wang Hui and Han Anguo, and Minyue's king Zou Ying is killed by his brother Zou Yushan, who then surrenders to the Han.
The Kingdom of Pergamum is deeded to Rome, Aristonicus starts a rebellion against this.
The Late Formative (or pre-Classic) period of the Maya civilization begins.
Having been freed by the Parthians, Demetrius II of Syria recovers the throne of the Seleucid Empire.
Scipio Aemilianus, victor of Carthage is possibly assassinated by his enemies in Rome.
The Kingdom of Pergamon becomes the Roman Province of Asia upon the defeat of Aristonicus, pretender to the Attalid throne, by M. Perperna.
The Han general Wei Qing, with an army of 30,000 cavalrymen, defeats a Xiongnu army north of Yanmen. The Han general Li Xi attacks the Xiongnu further to the east, riding out of Dai Prefecture.
The Han rationalize the northern frontier, abandoning the remote region of Zaoyang to the Xiongnu.
Having used the Xiongnu civil war to escape his imprisonment, the diplomat Zhang Qian returns to China and reports on the lands to the west.
Seleucus V Philometor succeeds his father Demetrius II as king of the Seleucid Empire. Due to his youth, his stepmother Cleopatra Thea acts as regent.
Tyre successfully revolts from the Seleucid Empire.
Completion of Aqua Tepula aqueduct in Rome.

In Rome, Marcus Fulvius Flaccus proposes the extension of Roman citizenship to the northern Italians, but the Senate reacts by sending him off to deal with disturbances around Massilia. And in so doing, commences the conquest of Transalpine Gaul.
In retaliation for the Han conquest of the Ordos Plateau two years prior, three Xiongnu forces raid the Prefectures of Dai, Dingxiang and Shang.
Cleopatra II of Egypt and her brother Ptolemy VIII of Egypt reconcile.
Emperor Wu of Han rewards Wei Qing by making him General-in-Chief.
Fregellae's revolt against Rome begins in Latium. Later the city is captured and destroyed by the Romans.
Emperor Wu of Han appoints Liu Ju, his son by Empress Wei Zifu, as Crown Prince.
Gracchus passes a law requiring the state to provide weapons and equipment for the soldiers in the Roman army.
A tribunal is established in Rome that executes 3,000 followers of Gracchus.

The rapid conquest of the Hexi Corridor provides the traditional western provinces of China with greater security. As a result, Emperor Wu halves the number of soldiers garrisoning the provinces of Longxi, Beidi and Shang.
The Teutons and the Cimbri migrate south and west to the Danube valley where they encounter the expanding Roman Republic.
Emperor Wu suspends further campaigning against the Xiongnu due to a shortage of horses.
Spring: Han Chinese forces under the General-in-Chief Wei Qing and the cavalry general Huo Qubing invade the Xiongnu Empire.
Emperor Wu of Han secretly executes his favourite necromancer Shao Weng for fraud.
The Roman colony of Narbo Martius is founded in Gallia Transalpina.
Ptolemy IX Philometor Soter II Lathyros becomes king of Egypt and claims the throne.
Marcus Aemilius Scaurus defeats the Carni Celtic tribes of Northern Italy, leading to their submission to Roman rule.
Parthia makes a trade treaty with China.
Horos, son of Haruotes, a resident of the temple of Isis in Egypt, attacked a worshiper at the temple.
Silk Road routes opened to traders and merchants, exporting goods from east to west.
Celtiberians lead a war against the Romans.
Germanic tribes attack Gaul and northern Iberia.
The state of Nanyue, a vassal of the Han dynasty, agrees to submit to Han laws and receives envoys to oversee the succession of the young king Zhao Xing.
Emperor Wu executes his favourite necromancer Luan Da for fraud.
The Roman Senate declares war against Jugurtha following the Siege of Cirta (ends 105 BC).
The city of Rome is devastated by fire.
Jugurtha, king of Numidia, defeats a Roman army under Aulus Postumius Albinus.
Emperor Wu of Han inspects the Han Empire, traveling 9,000 km. He also sends diplomats to search for the legendary Penglai Island.
Han campaigns against Dian: Emperor Wu launches a new campaign against the Dian Kingdom and establishes the Yizhou commandery in Yunnan during the dynasty's expansion southward.
The Han general Zhao Ponu and 700 cavalrymen are victorious in the Battle of Loulan in the Tarim Basin, capturing the king of Loulan in the first Han intervention west of the Hexi Corridor.
At Rome, the first official gladiator match is demonstrated by gladiators from Capua, as part of a training program for the military.
The Battle of Arausio, where the Cimbri destroy two Roman armies on the Rhône, is the most severe defeat of Roman forces since the Battle of Cannae.
The Han dynasty forms an alliance with the Wusun by marrying a Han princess to their king.
Alexander Jannaeus succeeds his brother Aristobulus I as king and high priest of Judea, until 76 BC.
Gaius Marius prepares a campaign against the Ambrones and Teutones (under king Teutobod) who are settled in Gaul.
Gandhara and Punjab are ruled by the Indo-Greek king Demetrius III Aniketos.
Han-Xiongnu War: the Han general Zhao Ponu escapes Xiongnu custody and returns to China.
Mural room in the Maya pyramid at San Bartolo, Guatemala, painted.

Emperor Wu of Han sends the Han general Gongsun Ao on a mission to rescue general Li Ling from Xiongnu captivity. Gongsun achieves little but receives incorrect information that Li has been training Xiongnu soldiers. Enraged, Emperor Wu exterminates Li's clan.
Sulla displays a lion hunt for the first time in games at Rome.
The Romans subdue the Maedi and Dardani.
Cyrene is left to the people of the Roman Republic by its ruler Ptolemy Apion.
Start of the Taishi era in the Han dynasty.
"Forty-metre structure" at Emain Macha (near modern Armagh, Northern Ireland) was built and destroyed, presumably for ritual or ceremonial purposes.
Ariobarzanes I Philoromaios becomes king of Cappadocia with Roman backing.
The Shakas start to control northwest India.
The first (failed) attempt to open a Latin rhetorical school.
End of era Taishi of Emperor Wu of Han China.
Gaius Sentius becomes Roman governor of Macedonia. He serves until 88 BC.
In the first diplomatic contact between Rome and Parthia, Sulla meets with a Parthian envoy, resulting in the parties recognizing the Euphrates as a common frontier.
Cicero starts to serve in the Roman army.
Corfinium in south-central Italy is the center of a rebellion against Rome.
The Etruscans are granted Roman citizenship.
Cicero ends his service in the Roman army.
Lex Pompeia grants Latin rights to cities in Cisalpine Gaul.
Pompeii is annexed by the Roman Republic.

Emperor Wu of Han makes preparations for the six-year-old Liu Fuling to be made Crown Prince and establishes Huo Guang as the future regent. The emperor executes Fuling's mother Lady Gouyi so that she cannot dominate the state while Fuling is a child emperor.
The Dardani, Scordisci, and the Maedi attack the Roman province of Macedonia.
The Social War ends with the defeat of the Italian allies by the Romans.
The eight-year-old Liu Fuling becomes emperor, with Huo Guang General-in-Chief and regent.
Siege of Athens (87–86 BC) ends when Sulla captures Athens from the Pontic army, removing the tyrant Aristion.
Battle of Cana: The Arab Nabataean Kingdom decisively defeats the Greek Seleucid Empire, slaying King Antiochus XII Dionysus, at modern-day Umm Qais in Jordan.
A fire breaks out which burns down the Temple of Jupiter (Jupiter Capitolinus) and destroys the collection of Sibylline Books.
Two new buildings were completed on the Capitoline Hill in Rome: the Temple of Jupiter Optimus Maximus and the Tabularium.
Pompeii becomes the Roman colony Colonia Cornelia Veneria Pompei when Sulla occupies the city with at least 4,000 soldier-colonizers.
Ptolemy XII Auletes succeeds Ptolemy XI Alexander II to the throne of Egypt.
Cicero travels to Athens and then to Rhodes to continue his studies of philosophy and oratory.
Julius Caesar returns to Rome after about two years of service in the army
In the Roman province of Hispania Citerior a republican army under Pompey the Great defeats an army of Sertorian rebels at the Battle of Valentia.
Julius Caesar travels to Rhodes and is taken captive by pirates
Nicomedes IV, last king of Bithynia bequeaths his kingdom to the Roman Senate upon his death (75/4 BC)

Spartacus moves north again, to cross the Alps into Gaul and then to Thracia. Outside Mutina on the plain of the River Po he defeats the Roman forces under Gaius Cassius Longinus, governor of Gallia Cisalpina.
The Suebi and other tribes under King Ariovistus invade Gaul.
Nessebar in modern-day Bulgaria comes under Roman rule.
In Rome, Cicero prosecutes former governor Verres; Verres exiles himself to Marseille before the trial is over.
Gaius Julius Caesar is a quaestor in Spain.
Kydonia, an ancient city on the island of Crete falls to Roman military forces.
Parthians and Romans re-establish Euphrates as a frontier.
Ostia, the harbour city of Ancient Rome, is sacked by pirates. The port is set on fire and the consular war fleet is destroyed.
Tribune of the plebs Gaius Antius Restio passes the Lex Antia sumptuaria law forbidding Roman magistrates from attending banquets.
Julius Caesar marries Pompeia, a granddaughter of Sulla
Julius Caesar reconciles with Pompey and Crassus
The army of the Han dynasty Chinese commander Zheng Ji is victorious over the Xiongnu in the Battle of Jushi.
Tigranes II is forced to surrender, by a payment of 6,000 talents, and is reinstated by Pompey as a "friend of the Roman people" to hold Armenia as a buffer zone.
In response to the illegal exercise of citizen rights by foreigners, the Roman Senate passes the Lex Papia, which expels all foreigners from Rome
Pompey the Great subjugates the kingdom of Iberia and makes Colchis a Roman province.
Tigranes of Armenia is defeated and captured by Pompey, thus ending all hostilities on the northeastern frontier of Rome.
King Antiochus XIII Asiaticus is deposed and killed by the Syrian chieftain Sampsiceramus I – this is considered by some the end of the Seleucid dynasty.
Pompey annexes Syria and captures Jerusalem, annexing Judea.
Pompey destroys the kingdom of Pontus; king Mithridates VI commits suicide after escaping to the Crimea.
Massacre of over 12,000 Jews on the Temple Mount in Jerusalem by Roman troops, in support of John Hyrcanus II against Aristobulus II.
Pompey conquers the people of Phonecia, Coele-Syria, and Judea for the Roman Republic.

Roman annexation of the Seleucid Empire and of Judea as a client kingdom. King Judah Aristobulus II removed from power, while his brother John Hyrcanus II is reappointed king (ethnarch) under Roman suzerainty and high priest, until 40 BC.
Cicero delivers his Pro Archia Poeta in defense of Aulus Licinius Archias' claim to Roman citizenship.
The forces of the conspirator Catiline are defeated by the loyal Roman armies of Antonius Hybrida led by Marcus Petreius in the Battle of Pistoria.
Pompey returns to Rome with a triumph in honor of his victories in the eastern provinces.
Creation of the First Triumvirate, an informal political alliance between Julius Caesar, Pompey the Great and Marcus Licinius Crassus (or 59 BC).
Gaius Julius Caesar suppresses an uprising and conquers all of Lusitania for Rome.
The Seleucid Empire comes to an end with the last two emperors being murdered on orders from Rome.

Caesar makes the gazette Acta Diurna (Daily News) public. The Acta contains details of official decrees and appointments; births, deaths, and marriages. Even sport results—the outcome of the gladiatorial contests and chariot races at the capital.
The colonia of Florentia, modern Florence, founded.
Base year of the Vikrama Era, founded by Vikrama, king of Ujjain in India.
First year of Julius Caesar's Gallic Wars:
Battle of the Sabis: Caesar defeats the Nervii, Roman forces are almost annihilated in an ambush.
Julius Caesar raises a further two legions (Legio XIII and Legio XIV), bringing his army in Gaul to eight legions (at which strength it remains until 54 BC).
Second year of Julius Caesar's Gallic Wars:

Julius Caesar leads an attack on the Morini and the Menapii tribes of the Belgae on the North Sea. They withdraw into their forests, creating difficulties for Caesar's supply lines. The onset of bad weather forces him to pull back into Gallia Belgica.
Third year of Julius Caesar's Gallic Wars:

This year, or possibly the following year, the king of the Trinovantes called Imanuentius, is overthrown and killed by his rival Cassivellaunus. His son Mandubracius flees to Gaul and appeals to Julius Caesar for help.
Fourth year of Julius Caesar's Gallic Wars:
Julius Caesar starts the season campaigning in Illyricum (in the Balkan region) against the Pirustae, who have been raiding Roman territory.

Pompey's Theater, the first permanent (non-wooden) theatre in Rome is built. Built of stone on the Field of Mars, it included a temple to Venus Victorious, a public courtyard, and a meeting hall or curia in the far end near the "Sacred Area".
Fifth year of Julius Caesar's Gallic Wars:
Pompey builds the first permanent theatre in Rome.
Second of Caesar's Invasions of Britain: Julius Caesar receives nominal submission from the tribal chief Cassivellaunus and installs Mandubracius as a friendly king.
Crassus sacks the Temple of Hierapolis and the Temple in Jerusalem on his way to engage the Parthians.
Julius Caesar suppresses a revolt led by Ambiorix near Sabis (Northern Gaul).
Vercingetorix, an Arverni chieftain, leads a revolt against Caesar in Central Gaul.
Battle of the Vingeanne: Julius Caesar rebuffs, with his German auxiliaries, a Gallic cavalry attack of Vercingetorix.
Julius Caesar crosses Mons Cevenna (central Gaul) and sends his army through the passes covered with snowdrifts to take the rebellious Arverni by surprise.
The Xiongnu split into two hordes. The Eastern horde is subject to China.
The Roman Republic takes control of Judea.
The Roman artillery piece called Scorpio is invented.
The Senate recalls Julius Caesar and rescinds his authority. Caesar breaks alliance with Pompey.
Caesar leads his army across the Rubicon, which separates his jurisdiction in Cisalpine Gaul from that of the Senate in Rome, and thus initiates a civil war.
Caesar's Civil War: Forces loyal to Julius Caesar led by Gaius Scribonius Curio were defeated by Pompeian Republicans under Publius Attius Varus and King Juba I of Numidia.
The Roman Senate receives a proposal from Julius Caesar that he and Pompey should lay down their commands simultaneously. The Senate responds that Caesar must immediately surrender his command.
Battle of Pharsalus: Julius Caesar decisively defeats Pompey at Pharsalus, who flees to Egypt. Pompey's army by and large is pardoned.
Pompey was killed by Lucius Septimius at Pelusium in Egypt.
The Roman temple to Bellona on the Capitolinus outside Rome is burnt to the ground.
Yuan becomes emperor of the Han Dynasty (until 33 BC).
Caesar's invasion of Africa, against Metellus Scipio and Labienus, Caesar's former lieutenant in Gaul.
Feng Yuan becomes consort to Emperor Yuan of the Han Dynasty.
Julius Caesar returns to Rome and is dictator for a year.
Caesar's erstwhile mistress, Queen Cleopatra VII of Egypt, and his son by her, Caesarion, take up residence in one of the dictator's estates on the Tiber.
Consuls: Gaius Julius Caesar, Marcus Aemilius Lepidus.
Julius Caesar dedicated the Temple of Venus Genetrix in Rome to Venus, the mythical ancestor of his family.
Julius Caesar establishes Julia Paterna Arelate as a colony in Gaul for veterans of the Sixth Legion, at the present day site of Arles.
Caesar is named dictator for life.
End of the Roman Civil War.
The Julian calendar takes effect as the civil calendar of the Roman Empire, establishing a solar calendar that is based on the Egyptian calendar of the day.

(the Ides of March) – Julius Caesar, dictator of Rome, is assassinated by a group of senators, amongst them Gaius Cassius Longinus, Marcus Junius Brutus, and Caesar's Massilian naval commander, Decimus Brutus.
Antony is granted a five-year governorship of northern and central Transalpine Gaul (France) and Cisalpine Gaul (Northern Italy).
Julius Caesar, the dictator of the Roman Republic, was stabbed to death by a group of senators led by Marcus Junius Brutus.
Pharaoh Cleopatra VII of Egypt declares her son co-ruler as Ptolemy XV Caesarion.
According to legend, Nagasena creates the Emerald Buddha figurine in Patna, India.
Cicero, widely considered one of ancient Rome's greatest orators and prose stylists, was killed after having been proscribed as an enemy of the state.
Forces led by Mark Antony fought the Battle of Mutina against those of Decimus Brutus, one of Julius Caesar's assassins.
Octavian is first proclaimed imperator by his troops.
War of Mutina: Despite initial success, troops loyal to Mark Antony were defeated near the Via Aemilia in northern Italy by legions loyal to the Roman Senate.
Octavian returns to Rome and arranges for ± 40,000 veterans' settlements in Campania, Etruria, Picenum, Samnium, Umbria, and in northern Italy.
Athenodorus, a philosopher, encounters a ghost in Athens. This popular story is one of the first poltergeist stories in history.

Parthians conquer Jerusalem. Hyrcanus II is removed from power, while Antigonus the Hasmonean becomes king of Judea under Parthian rule. Herod the Great flees Jerusalem to Rome. There he is titled king of Judea by Mark Antony.
The Ji Jiu Pian dictionary, published about this year during the Han dynasty, is the earliest known reference to the hydraulic-powered trip hammer device.

Sextus Pompey, controls Sicily, Sardinia, Corsica and the Peloponnesus, and is recognized by the Triumvirate in the Pact of Misenum. The pact helps to assure Rome's grain supply, and the blockade on Roman Italy is lifted.

Octavian appoints Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa governor of Transalpine Gaul, where he puts down an uprising of the Aquitanians. He also fights successfully against the Germanic tribes, and becomes the next Roman general to cross the Rhine after Julius Caesar.
The kingdom of Goguryeo in Korea is founded by the king Dongmyeong.
Judea: Aristobulus III, the last of the Hasmoneans, becomes High Priest in Jerusalem, replacing Ananelus, who has only held the position for one year.
The Sicilian revolt against the Second Triumvirate of the Roman Republic ended when the fleet of Sextus Pompey, the rebel leader, was defeated at the Battle of Naulochus.
Azes I, Indo-Scythian ruler, completes the domination of the Scythians in northern India.
Illyria becomes a Roman province. Gaius Julius Caesar Octavian conducts a rendezvous with the Roman fleet under Agrippa, which is engaged in clearing the Dalmatian coast of piracy.

Pannonia is attacked by Octavian Caesar, who conquers and sacks the stronghold Siscia (Sisak) of the Segestani, which is taken after a 30-day siege. The country is not definitely subdued, however, until 9 BC.
Antony advances into Armenia with an expeditionary force (16 legions) and marches to the capital Artaxata. He arrests king Artavasdes II and takes him to Alexandria.
Crown Prince Ao ascends to the throne as Emperor Cheng of Han of the Han dynasty (until 7 BC).
Mark Antony annexes the kingdom of Media and arranges the marriage of his son Alexander Helios with princess Iotapa, the daughter of king Artavasdes I.
Final War of the Roman Republic: Mark Antony transfers his headquarters from Samos to Athens, where he assembles a fleet of 500 combat vessels and 300 transport ships, crewed by 150,000 men.
Octavian (32 years old) takes court at Samos. After his decisive victory at Actium he builds Nicopolis; the city is populated by Greeks from settlements further inland.
Roman Civil War: Battle of Actium: Off the western coast of Greece, Octavian Caesar defeats naval forces under Mark Antony and Cleopatra VII.
The remaining children of Cleopatra are spared by Octavian and taken back in triumph; Octavia Minor raises Alexander Helios, Cleopatra Selene and Ptolemy Philadelphus in her household in Rome.
War of Actium: Octavian defeated the forces of Mark Antony and Cleopatra at Alexandria, establishing Roman Egypt.

Octavian Caesar becomes Roman Consul for the fifth time. His partner is Sextus Appuleius. He is granted the title of imperator, and for the third time in Roman history the doors of the Temple of Janus are closed, signalling peace.
Octavian celebrates, in Rome, three triumphs on consecutive days (August 13, August 14, and August 15) to commemorate his victories in Illyricum, Actium and Egypt.
Sofia, modern day capital of Bulgaria, is conquered by the Romans and becomes known as Ulpia Serdica.
Augustus initiates a census of the Roman Republic for the first time since 69 BC.
Chinese astronomers during the Han dynasty made the first precisely dated observation of a sunspot.
Gaius Julius Caesar Octavian becomes Roman Consul for the sixth time. His partner Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa becomes Consul for the second time.
The earliest dated record of a sunspot by Chinese astronomers.
Augustus' first census of the Roman Empire (formerly the Roman Republic) reports a total of 4,063,000 citizens.
Gaius Julius Caesar Octavian becomes Roman Consul for the seventh time. His partner Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa becomes Consul for the third time.
Gaius Octavianus was given the titles Augustus and Princeps by the Roman Senate when he became the first Roman emperor.

Octavian formally returns full power to the Senate; they give him the titles of Princeps and Augustus. He accepts this honor, having declined the alternative title of Romulus, thus becoming first Roman emperor.
Gavius Silo, orator, is heard by Caesar Augustus - mentioned by Seneca.

Imperator Caesar Augustus becomes Roman Consul for the eighth time. His partner Titus Statilius Taurus becomes Consul for the second time and refounds the old Contestanian Iberian capital of Ilici (Elche), known since then as "Colonia Iulia Ilici Augusta".
The Andhra dynasty replaces the Kanva dynasty, and rules over the eastern part of India.
Estimation: Rome, capital of the Roman Empire, becomes the largest city in the world, taking the lead from Chang'an, capital of China.
Imperator Caesar Augustus becomes Consul for the ninth time. His partner is Marcus Junius Silanus.
The Roman colony of Emerita Augusta is founded (present-day Mérida).
Augustus founds the city of Nicopolis in Egypt to commemorate his final victory over Mark Antony.
Caesar Augustus becomes Roman Consul for the tenth time. His partner is Gaius Norbanus Flaccus.
In response to Meroë's incursions into Upper Egypt, the Roman legions move south and raze Napata. (History of Sudan).
The Nubians, led by queen Kandake Amanirenas, take the initiative against the Roman Empire, and attack the Roman province of Egypt moving towards Elephantine.
The Roman poet Horace publishes the first three books of Odes.
King Artaxias II returns, with the support of the Parthians, to Armenia and claims the throne. Artavasdes I escapes to Rome, where Caesar Augustus receives him.
The Roman governor of Egypt, Gaius Petronius, marches up the Nile with legions XXII Deiotariana and III Cyrenaica, and destroys the Nubian capital of Napata.
Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa divorces Claudia Marcella Major, and marries Julia the Elder, daughter of Caesar Augustus.
After 20 years, Emperor Augustus initiates his second census of the Roman Empire.
Emperor Ai becomes the emperor of Han China.
Sextilis, the eighth month of the early Julian calendar, is renamed Augustus (August) by a decree of the Roman Senate in honor of Augustus.
Germanic Wars: An alliance of Germanic tribes led by Arminius engaged Roman forces at the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest, defeating three legions within a few days.
The Western Han dynasty of China ended after the throne was usurped by Wang Mang, who founded the Xin dynasty.
Emperor Augustus abandons his plan to create a defensive border at the Elbe, in order to reinforce the Roman defenses along the Rhine and the Danube.
Emperor Augustus initiates his third census of the Roman Empire after 20 years.
The Euthydemid dynasty, a Greek dynasty in Bactria, is brought to an end.
Liu Xiu proclaimed himself the monarch of the Han dynasty as Emperor Guangwu.
Emperor Tiberius is a Roman Consul for the fourth time.
Greek geographer Strabo publishes Geographica, a work covering the world known to the Romans and Greeks at the time of Emperor Augustus – it is the only such book to survive from the ancient world.
Liu Xuan, a descendant of the Han dynasty royal family and leader of insurgents against the Xin dynasty, proclaims himself emperor against Wang Mang.
After the death of Emperor Gongsun Shu of Chengjia, the empire was conquered by the Eastern Han dynasty.
Emperor Tiberius founds a credit bank in Rome.
Naevius Sutorius Macro gains favour in the Roman Empire by prostituting his wife Ennia Thrasylla to Caligula.
Roman emperor Caligula was murdered by Cassius Chaerea and other members of the Praetorian Guard, who proclaimed Claudius to be the new emperor.
Emperor Claudius and future emperor Titus Flavius Vespasianus become Roman Consuls.
Start of Yongping era of the Chinese Han dynasty.
The Yuejue Shu, the first known gazetteer of China, is written during the Han Dynasty.
Emperor Claudius and future emperor Titus Flavius Vespasianus become Roman Consuls.
Start of Yongping era of the Chinese Han dynasty.
The Yuejue Shu, the first known gazetteer of China, is written during the Han Dynasty.
Gaius Suetonius Paulinus, Roman governor of Britain, captures the island of Mona (Anglesey), the last stronghold of the Druids.
Paul's Epistle to the Philippians is written from Rome.
The Roxolani are defeated on the Danube by the Romans.
Gaius Suetonius Paulinus, Roman governor of Britain, captures the island of Mona (Anglesey), the last stronghold of the Druids.
A violent storm destroys 200 ships anchored at Portus.
Nero completes the Baths of Nero in Rome.
Paul of Tarsus is released from imprisonment in Rome.
Pompeii was severely damaged by a strong earthquake, which may have been a precursor to the eruption of Mount Vesuvius that destroyed the town 17 years later.
According to legend, Joseph of Arimathea goes to Glastonbury on the first Christian mission to Britain.
First Epistle of Peter written from Babylon according to traditional Christian belief.
Persecution of Christians in Rome begins under Nero. Peter the Apostle is possibly among those crucified.
In China, the first official reference to Buddhism is made.
The first Christian community in Africa is founded by Mark, a disciple of Peter.
Paul in Asia Minor for second time after his release from Rome. Then probably goes to Greece. Second imprisonment in Rome.

The Jewish Revolt commences against the Roman Empire. The Zealots lay siege to Jerusalem and annihilate the Roman garrison (a cohort of Legio III Cyrenaica). The Sicarii capture the fortress of Masada overlooking the Dead Sea.
The Roman Legio II Augusta is stationed at Gloucester.
First Jewish–Roman War: Vespasian arrives in Ptolemais in Phoenicia along with the Legio X Fretensis and Legio V Macedonica, to put down the revolt.
Gaius Julius Vindex revolts, first in a series of revolts that lead to Nero's downfall.
Linus succeeds Peter, as the second Bishop of Rome.
Emperor Nero commits suicide four miles outside Rome. He is deserted by the Praetorian Guard, and then stabs himself in the throat.
Final year that Tacitus records Annals, a written history of the Roman Empire.
The Roman Senate accepts Servius Sulpicius Galba, as Roman Emperor.
After defeat by Vitellius' troops at Bedriacum, Roman emperor Otho killed himself.
Otho seizes power in Rome, proclaims himself emperor, and reigns for three months before committing suicide.
The Roman legions in Germania Superior refuse to swear loyalty to Galba. They rebel and proclaim Vitellius as emperor.
Tiberius Julius Alexander orders his legions in Alexandria to swear allegiance to Vespasian as emperor.
First Jewish–Roman War: Roman forces led by Titus set fire to the Second Temple during the siege of Jerusalem.
Later Roman emperor Domitian marries Domitia Longina.
Romans make a punitive expedition against the Garamantes – they are forced to have an official relationship with the Roman Empire.
Ze-Hakèlé (Zoskales in Greek) becomes king of Aksum.
Doncaster is founded by Roman settlers. The area was originally known as Danum.
Herodium, a Jewish fortress south of Jerusalem, is conquered and destroyed by Legio X Fretensis on their way to Masada.
Mithraism begins to spread throughout the Roman Empire.
Antiochus IV of Syria is deposed by Emperor Vespasian.

First Jewish–Roman War: The Roman army (Legio X Fretensis) under Sextus Lucilius Bassus lays siege to the Jewish garrison of Machaerus at the Dead Sea. After they capitulate, the Zealots are allowed to leave the fortress before it is destroyed.
Vespasian and Titus are Roman Consuls.
Emperor Vespasian begins conquest of territory east of the upper Rhine and south of the Main. In addition, he reorganizes the defenses of the upper and lower Danube.

The Chinese Han dynasty launches a major campaign against the Xiongnu, whom they confront in the Battle of Yiwulu in the Kumul oasis, an ultimate Han military victory led by General Dou Gu (d. AD 88).
Titus Flavius Domitianus becomes Roman Consul.
Emperor Ming of Han appoints Chen Mu to the revived office of Protector of the Western Regions.
Emperor Vespasian and his son Titus Caesar Vespasianus become Roman Consuls.
The Black Forest region is reattached to the Roman Empire.
Accession of Han Zhangdi of the Han dynasty (until AD 88).
Emperor Vespasian and his son Titus Caesar Vespasianus become Roman Consuls.
The Temple of Peace, also known as the Forum of Vespasian, is built in Rome. The temple celebrates the conquest of Jerusalem (in AD 70) and houses the Menorah from Herod's Temple.
Emperors Vespasianus Augustus and Titus Caesar Vespasianus become Roman Consuls.
First year of Jianchu era of the Chinese Han dynasty. (Clarification needed as to the meaning of this)
Pope Anacletus I succeeds Pope Linus as the third pope of the Catholic Church (according to the official Vatican list).
Agricola conquers Anglesey, and disperses his army to their winter quarters.
Pliny the Elder publishes the first ten books of Naturalis Historia.
The Romans develop a simple method of distillation.
Emperor Kadphises of the Kushan Empire sends a delegation to Rome, to seek support against the Parthians.
Indian Prince Aji Caka introduces the Sanskrit language and Pallawa script, used to inscribe Javanese words and phrases, to the Indonesian islands.
The Romans conquer the Ordovices, located in present-day northern Wales, as well as the Silures.
Chester is founded as a castrum or Roman fort with the name Deva Victrix. The fortress is built by Legio II Adiutrix and contains barracks, granaries, military baths and headquarters.
Mamucium (the first Manchester) is founded as a frontier fort and settlement in the North West of England, a distance to the north of Chester.
Vespasianus Augustus and Titus Caesar Vespasianus become Roman Consuls.
Domitian, the last Flavian emperor of Rome, was confirmed by the Senate to succeed his brother Titus.
Pliny the Younger is flamen Divi Augusti (priest in the cult of the Emperor).
Dio Chrysostom is banished from Rome, Italy, and Bithynia, after advising one of the Emperor's conspiring relatives.
Domitian is, again, also a Roman Consul.
In Rome, the castration of slaves is prohibited.
The Roman fort Inchtuthil is built in Scotland.
Change from Jianchu to Yuanhe era of the Chinese Eastern Han Dynasty.
Emperor Domitian recalls Agricola back to Rome, where he is rewarded with a triumph and the governorship of the Roman province of Africa, but he declines it.
The construction of the limes, a line of Roman fortifications from the Rhine to the Danube, has begun.
Dacians under Decebalus engage in two wars against the Romans from this year to AD 88 or 89.
Emperor Domitian repulses a Dacian invasion of Moesia.
Ban Gu (Pan Kou) and his sister Ban Zhao (Pan Tchao) compose the History of China.
Emperor Domitian introduces the Capitoline Games.
Roman general (and future emperor) Trajan begins a campaign to crush an uprising in Germania.
Lyon, a city in Gaul, has a population of over 100,000 citizens.
Sextus Julius Sparsus gains power in the Roman Senate.
The Roman Julius Maternus explores western Africa.
Last year (4th) of yuanhe era and start of zhanghe era of the Chinese Eastern Han dynasty.
The First Dacian War ends: Decebalus becomes a client king of Rome, he receives money, craftsmen and war machines to protect the borders (limes) of the Roman Empire.
Two Egyptian obelisks are erected in Benevento in front of the Temple of Isis, in honour of Emperor Domitian.
Battle of Ikh Bayan: The Han Chinese army under Dou Xian, allied with the southern Xiongnu, is victorious over the Northern Xiongnu.
First year of Yongyuan era of the Chinese Han dynasty.
The Young Flavian Woman is made. It is now kept at Musei Capitolini, Rome.
Manius Acilius Glabrio and Marcus Ulpius Traianus become Roman Consuls.
Rome is described by Statius in his poems.
Emperor Domitian becomes a Roman Consul.
The Roman army moves into Mesopotamia (modern Syria).
Domitian banishes all Stoic philosophers from Rome.
Emperor Domitian rebuilds and rededicates the Curia Julia (meeting place of the Roman Senate), which had burned down in AD 64.
The Chinese General Ban Chao completes his conquest of the Tarim Basin by taking Yānqi, which is located on the strategic Silk Road.
Emperor Domitian and Titus Flavius Clemens become Roman Consuls.
A schism in Buddhism creates a new, popular religion in India, Mahâyâna ("Great Vehicle").

Nerva is declared emperor by the Roman Senate as the new ruler of the Roman Empire. He recalls citizens exiled by Domitian; this is the beginning of the Era of the Five Good Emperors. The Antonines Dynasty starts.
Nerva, the first of the "Five Good Emperors" of ancient Rome, came to power following the assassination of his predecessor Domitian.
The Arch of Titus is completed in Rome.
Emperor Nerva recalls his general Marcus Ulpius Trajanus, age 44, from the German frontier and is forced by the Praetorian Guard to adopt him as his successor.
Gloucester, England is founded as Colonia Glevum Nervensis by the Romans.
The Roman colony of Cuicul is started in Numidia.
Emperor Nerva suffers a stroke during a private audience.
The silver content of the Roman denarius rises to 93 percent under emperor Trajan, up from 92 percent under Domitian.
Trajan succeeded his adoptive father Nerva as Roman emperor; the Roman Empire reached its maximum extent under his rule.
Emissaries of the Kushan Empire reach the Roman Empire.
Pope Evaristus succeeds Pope Clement I as the fifth pope according to Roman Catholic tradition.
Bricks become the primary building material in the Roman Empire.
In China, the wheelbarrow makes its first appearance.
Titus Avidius Quietus' rule as governor of Roman Britain ends.
Emperor Trajan starts an expedition against Dacia, exceeding the limits of the Roman Empire set by Augustus.
Third Battle of Tapae: Roman forces, led by Trajan, defeat the Dacian king Decebalus in Transylvania.
Emperor Trajan returns to Rome after a successful campaign against Dacia, through which he reestablishes clear Roman sovereignty over King Decebalus.
A fire breaks out in Rome.
In India, figures of Buddha replace abstract motifs on decorative items.
Last year (17th) of yongyuan era and start of yuanxing era of the Chinese Eastern Han dynasty.
Pope Alexander I succeeds Pope Evaristus as the sixth pope according to Roman Catholic tradition.
The Romans conquer Kerak from the Nabateans.
Emperor Trajan conquers the Dacian Fortresses of the Orăştie Mountains, and surrounds the capital, Sarmizegetusa.
Romans construct a road between Eilat and Damascus.
The Bostran era, the official era of the Roman province of Arabia Petraea, began.
The region of Dacia, comprising parts of modern Romania, became a province of the Roman Empire.
The south-eastern part of Dacia (modern Romania) becomes a Roman province: Roman Dacia. The veterans of the legions are given land in the new province for their service in the Roman army.
An Indian ambassador is received by Emperor Trajan.
First year of the yongchu era of the Chinese Eastern Han Dynasty.
Liu Hu becomes Emperor An of Han.
Appius Annius Trebonius Gallus and Marcus Atilius Bradua become Roman Consuls.
Osroes I of Parthia succeeds his brother Pacorus II, and rules over the western Parthian Empire.
The Aqua Traiana is inaugurated by Emperor Trajan; the aqueduct channels water from Lake Bracciano, 40 km northwest of Rome.
The Via Traiana is constructed at the Emperor Trajan's personal expense; the road connects Benevento with Brundisium (Brindisi).

Caravans make regular departures from Luoyang with Chinese ginger, cassia (a type of cinnamon), and silk to be bartered in Central Asia for gold, silver, glassware, pottery, cloth, and intaglio gems from Rome.
The Forum of Trajan is constructed in Rome, by the Syrian architect Apollodorus of Damascus.
The Roman Empire has more than 75,000 km of roads.
Emperor Trajan sends Pliny the Younger to be governor (legatus Augusti) of Bithynia.
Emperor Trajan sails from Rome to begin his expedition against Parthia. He arrives in Athens where Parthian envoys greet him with olive branches, a sign of peace.
Last (7th) year of Yongchu era of the Chinese Eastern Han Dynasty.
Trajan's Column near the Colosseum in Rome is completed to commemorate the Emperor's victory over the Dacians in the Second Dacian War.
A monument to Philopappos, prince-in-exile of old Commagene (a buffer-state between Rome and Parthia) is erected in Athens.
First year of Yuanchu era of the Chinese Eastern Han dynasty.
The kingdom of Osroene becomes a vassal kingdom of the Roman Empire.
Alexandria in Egypt is damaged during the Jewish-Greek civil wars. Marcus Rutilius Lupus, the Roman governor, sends Legio XXII Deiotariana to protect the inhabitants of Memphis.
Pope Sixtus I succeeds Alexander I as the seventh pope of Rome (according to Catholic biographies).
The Diaspora Revolt erupts almost simultaneously across various Jewish Diaspora communities in the empire's east, including Egypt, Libya and Cyprus.
Emperor Trajan completes his invasion of Parthia by capturing the cities of Seleucia, Babylon, Ctesiphon and Susa, marking the high-water mark of the Roman Empire's eastern expansion.
Trajan makes Syria a province of Rome and crosses the Tigris to annex Adiabene. He proceeds with his army to the Persian Gulf and conquers territory that becomes the province of Parthia.
Trajan sends laureatae to the Roman Senate on account of his victories and being conqueror of Parthia.
Construction begins on the Pantheon in Rome.
John I becomes the 7th Bishop of Jerusalem.
The silver content of the Roman denarius falls to 87 percent under emperor Hadrian, down from 93 percent in the reign of Trajan.
Emperor Hadrian is also a Roman Consul.
Osroene is returned to native rule by the Roman Empire.
Pantheon, in Rome, starts to be built.

Emperor Hadrian stations Legio VI Victrix in Roman Britain, to assist in quelling the resistance of a local rebellion. The legion is key in securing the victory, and eventually replaces Legio IX Hispana at Eboracum.
Reign in Northern India by Nahapana, Scythian king. He attacks the kingdom of Andhra and annexes Southern Rajputana.
Foss Dyke is constructed in Britain.
The Scythians dominate western India: Punjab, Sind, the north of Gujarat and a portion of central India.
Emperor Hadrian fixes the border between Roman Britain and Caledonia, on a line running from the River Tyne to the Solway Firth.
Era name changes from Yongning (2nd year) to Jianguang in the Chinese Eastern Han dynasty.(Needs clarification or deletion)
Roman settlement in present-day Wiesbaden, Germany, is first mentioned.

Emperor Hadrian orders that a 73-mile (117-kilometer) wall be built to mark the northern Roman Empire while personally visiting the area. Hadrian's Wall, as it comes to be known, is intended to keep the Caledonians, Picts and other tribes at bay.
Vindolanda, a Roman auxiliary fort (castrum) in northern England, is garrisoned by cohort VIII Batavorum.
Emperor Hadrian averts a war with Parthia by a personal meeting with Osroes I (according to the Historia Augusta, disputed).
Hadrian leads a punitive campaign against Berbers who had been raiding Roman towns in Roman Mauretania.
In China, Ban Yong, son of Ban Chao, reestablishes the Chinese control over the Tarim Basin.
Antinous becomes Hadrian's beloved companion on his journeys through the Roman Empire.
Emperor Hadrian begins to rebuild the Olympeion in Athens.
Change of emperor of the Chinese Han dynasty from Han Andi to Marquis of Beixiang, then to Han Shundi.
Gautamiputra Satakarni, a king of the Andhra dynasty, conquers the Konkan near Bombay. He then controls central India from coast to coast.
Last (4th) year of the Yanguang era of the Chinese Han dynasty.
First year of the Yongjian era of the Chinese Han dynasty.
The old Pantheon is demolished by Emperor Hadrian, and the construction of a new one begins (its date is uncertain, because Hadrian chooses not to inscribe the temple).
Emperor Hadrian returns to Rome, after a seven-year voyage to the Roman provinces.
Kanishka I starts to rule in the Kushan Empire.
The philosopher Carpocrates rejects ownership of private property as being un-Christian.
Roman agriculture declines, as imports from Egypt and North Africa depress wheat prices, making it unprofitable to farm, and forcing many farmers off the land.
Roman bakeries produce dozens of bread varieties, and the Romans distribute free bread for the poor.
The Pantheon in Rome is finished.
Change of Patriarch of Constantinople, from Patriarch Diogenes to Eleutherius.
Emperor Hadrian continues his voyages, now inspecting Caria, Cappadocia and Syria.
A law is passed in Rome banning the execution of slaves without a trial.
Huviska becomes king of the Kushan Empire in India.
The Temple of Olympian Zeus is completed at Athens.
Emperor Hadrian builds the city Aelia Capitolina, on the location of Jerusalem.

Bar Kokhba revolt: The messianic, charismatic Jewish leader Simon bar Kokhba starts a war of liberation for Judea against the Romans, which is eventually crushed (in 135) by Emperor Hadrian; Rabbi Akiva is supportive of the rebellion.

Merchants in Britain build structures outside the forts of Hadrian's Wall, and offer goods and services (including brothels) to Roman soldiers, who receive salaries in a region that otherwise has virtually no ready money.
The Temple of Olympian Zeus (Athens) is completed, using Cossutius' design.
A law improving the lot of free workers is passed in Rome.
Arrianus, Roman governor of Cappadocia, repulses an attack of the Alani, a nomadic tribe from southeastern Russia.
The Romans retake Jerusalem. The largely-destroyed city is renamed Aelia Capitolina.
A Jewish diaspora begins, as Emperor Hadrian bars Jews from Jerusalem, and has survivors of the massacre dispersed across the Roman Empire. Many join Mediterranean ports.
Jerusalem is renamed Colonia Aelia Capitolina, in honor of Hadrian. Legio VI Ferrata rebuilds the legionary fortress in the city, and constructs a Roman temple at Golgotha.
Last (4th) year of Yangjia era of the Chinese Han Dynasty.
First year of Yonghe era of the Chinese Han Dynasty.
Hadrian dictates his memoirs at his villa near Tivoli (Tibur) outside Rome.
Pope Hyginus succeeds Pope Telesphorus as the ninth pope of Rome according to tradition.

In Jiaozhi (present-day northern Vietnam) during the Second Era of Northern Domination, a rebellion of the Cham people broke out and lasted for one year, until the peace agreement was made between the Han dynasty governors and the rebels in 138.
Antoninus Pius succeeds Hadrian as Roman Emperor, and asks the Senate to confer divine honors for Hadrian.
Roman emperor Hadrian adopted Antoninus Pius as his son and successor following the death of Hadrian's first adopted son Lucius Aelius.
The silver content of the Roman denarius falls to 75 percent under Emperor Antoninus Pius, down from 87 percent under Hadrian.
Antoninus Pius and Gaius Bruttius Praesens become Roman Consuls.
Marcus Aurelius is named Caesar. He marries the 9-year-old Faustina the Younger, daughter of Antoninus Pius.
Emperor Antoninus Augustus Pius and Marcus Aurelius Caesar become Roman Consuls.
Marcion arrives in Rome, bringing Evangelikon and Apostolikon to the Christian community.
Pope Pius I succeeds Pope Hyginus as the tenth pope of Rome according to tradition.
Change of Patriarch of Constantinople from Felix of Byzantium to Polycarpus II of Byzantium.
Last (6th) year of Yonghe era of the Chinese Han Dynasty.
The Temple of Antoninus and Faustina is constructed in Rome; the temple is dedicated to Empress Faustina the Elder.
First year of the Hanan era of the Chinese Han Dynasty.
Municipal doctors are named throughout the Roman Empire.
The Chinese Taoist alchemist Wei Boyang, author of the Kinship of the Three, is the first to describe an early form of gunpowder solution.
Antoninus Pius serves as Roman Consul.
The Roman doctor Antyllus performs the first arteriotomy.
Change of emperor from Han Shundi to Han Chongdi of the Han dynasty.
Reign of Huvishka, emperor of the Kushan Empire.
The Roman campaigns in Mauretania begin.
Antoninus Augustus Pius and Marcus Aurelius Caesar become Roman Consuls.
Change of emperor from Han Chongdi to Han Zhidi of the Chinese Han dynasty.
Faustina the Younger is given the title Augusta, and becomes Roman Empress.
Han Huandi succeeds Han Zhidi as emperor of the Chinese Han dynasty.
Festivals to celebrate the 900th anniversary of the founding of Rome begin.
First year of Jianhe of the Chinese Han Dynasty.
Marcus Aurelius receives imperial powers, from Emperor Antoninus Pius.
Emperor Antoninus Pius hosts a series of grand games, to celebrate Rome's 900th anniversary.
Euzois succeeds Athendodorus, as Patriarch of Constantinople.
First and only year of the "Heping" era of the Han dynasty in China.
Paper, made in China, arrives in Transoxiana.
The Middle Culture period of Mayan civilization ends.
Detail from a rubbing of a stone relief in Wu family shrine (Wuliangci), Jiaxiang, Shandong, is made (Han dynasty).
First year of Yuanjia of the Chinese Han dynasty.
Mytilene and Smyrna are destroyed by an earthquake.
The Chinese domination of the Tarim Basin weakens.
Minor uprisings occur in Roman Egypt against Roman rule.
King Eupator of Bosphorus pays tribute to Rome, due to the threat posed by the Alani.
Last (2nd) year of Yongxing era of the Chinese Han Dynasty.
The Council of Rome, a pre-ecumenical church council, is held and presided over by Bishop of Rome Anicetus.
The heresiarch Montanus first appears in Ardaban (Mysia).
A revolt against Roman rule begins in Dacia.

In Jiuzhen (modern day Northern Vietnam), during the second Era of Northern Domination, a rebellion led by Chu Đạt breaks out and lasts for two to three years, until it is quelled by the Han Dynasty, under emperor Huan.
A revolt against Roman rule in Dacia is crushed.
The earliest dated use of Sol Invictus, in a dedication from Rome.
In India, the reign of Shivashri Satakarni, as King Satavahana of Andhra, begins.
In Roman Empire, the Antonine Wall in Britain is retaken by Roman legions.
In Rome, the manufacturing of soap containing grease, lime and ashes begins.
The first Buddhist monks arrive in China.
The Parthians invade Armenia, and install their own candidate on the throne. A legion (perhaps Legio IX Hispana) is destroyed at Elegeia.
The silver content of the Roman denarius falls to 68 percent under Emperor Marcus Aurelius, down from 75 percent under Antoninus Pius.
Arrian, Greek historian and writer, publishes Indica, a work on India and its people.
Marcus Statius Priscus re-conquers Armenia; the capital city of Artaxata is ruined.
Ctesiphon is captured by the Romans, but returns to the Parthians after the end of the war.
Seleucia on the Tigris is destroyed.
The Antonine Wall in Scotland is abandoned by the Romans.
Antonine Plague: A pandemic breaks out in Rome, after the Roman army returns from Parthia. The plague significantly depopulates the Roman Empire and China.
Discourse to the Greek (Oratio ad Graecos), by the Syrian Tatian, is the first treatise on the evils of paganism in Christian literature.
The Romans establish a garrison at Doura Europos on the Euphrates, a control point for the commercial route to the Persian Gulf.
A plague (possibly small pox) comes from the East and spreads throughout the Roman Empire, lasting for roughly twenty years.
Pope Soter succeeds Pope Anicetus as the twelfth pope of Rome.

Scholars who have denounced eunuchs are arrested, killed or banished from the capital and official life in Han dynasty China. This is the first of the Disasters of the Partisan Prohibitions, which end in 184.
The Germans devastate the Balkans and ransack the sanctuary of Eleusis, near Athens.
Emperor Ling of Han succeeds Emperor Huan of Han as the emperor of the Chinese Han Dynasty; the first year of the Jianning era.
The Roman army crosses the Alps into Pannonia, and subdues the Marcomanni at Carnuntum, north of the Danube.
Galen moves back to Rome for good.
Marcomannic Wars: Germanic tribes invade the frontiers of the Roman Empire, specifically the provinces of Raetia and Moesia.
Emperor Marcus Aurelius writes in Sirmium (Pannonia) his first of 12 books of the Meditations in Koine Greek.
Marcus Aurelius orders humane treatment for Christians and slaves throughout the Roman Empire.
The Suebian tribes of the Marcomanni cross the Danube and invade Northern Italy. The Roman army (20,000 men) is destroyed near Carnuntum in Pannonia.
Armenia and Mesopotamia become protectorates of the Roman Empire.
Emperor Marcus Aurelius forms a new military command, the praetentura Italiae et Alpium. Aquileia is relieved, and the Marcomanni are evicted from Roman territory.
Marcus Aurelius signs a peace treaty with the Quadi and the Sarmatian Iazyges. The Germanic tribes of the Hasdingi (Vandals) and the Lacringi become Roman allies.
Battle of Jwawon: Goguryeo Prime Minister Myeongnim Dap-bu defeats the Chinese Han dynasty forces in Manchuria.
Last (5th) year of Jianning era and start of Xiping era of the Chinese Han dynasty.
The Bucolic War broke out in Egypt. The Egyptians, led by Isidorus, fought against the Roman Empire under Marcus Aurelius.
Given control of the Eastern Empire, Avidius Cassius, the governor of Syria, crushes an insurrection of shepherds known as the Boukoloi.
Meditations by Marcus Aurelius is written, in Greek, while on military campaigns in Pannonia.
Pope Eleuterus succeeds Pope Soter as the thirteenth pope.
Reign in India of Yajnashri Satakarni, Satavahana king of the Andhra. He extends his empire from the center to the north of India.
Commodus, son of Marcus Aurelius and his wife Faustina, is named Caesar.
Marcus Aurelius suppresses a revolt of Avidius Cassius, governor of Syria, after the latter proclaims himself emperor.
The end of the Bucolic War in Egypt.
Emperor Marcus Aurelius grants his son Commodus the rank of Imperator, and makes him Supreme Commander of the Roman legions.
Marcus Aurelius and Commodus enter Rome after a campaign north of the Alps, and receive a triumph for their victories over the Germanic tribes.
The Equestrian Statue of Marcus Aurelius is made. It is now kept at Museo Capitolini in Rome.
A systematic persecution of Christians begins in Rome; the followers take refuge in the catacombs.
Commodus is given the title Augustus, and is made co-emperor, with the same status as his father, Marcus Aurelius.
The churches in southern Gaul are destroyed after a crowd accuses the local Christians of practicing cannibalism.
In India, the decline of the Kushan Empire begins. The Sassanides take over Central Asia.
Last (7th) year of Xiping era and start of Guanghe era of the Chinese Han dynasty.
The Montanist heresy is condemned for the first time.

Marcus Aurelius drives the Marcomanni over the Danube and reinforces the border. To repopulate and rebuild a devastated Pannonia, Rome allows the first German colonists to enter territory controlled by the Roman Empire.
Roman legionaries of Legio II Adiutrix engrave on the rock of the Trenčín Castle (Slovakia) the name of the town Laugaritio, marking the northernmost point of Roman presence in that part of Europe.
The Roman fort Castra Regina ("fortress by the Regen river") is built at Regensburg, on the right bank of the Danube in Germany.
Northern British from beyond Hadrian's Wall invade the North of modern-day England, causing Emperor Commodus to allow swathes of Northern cities to establish city walls.
Rome creates a 4-mile wide buffer zone by the Danube.
Twelve Christian inhabitants of Scillium in Numidia are executed in Carthage (also in North Africa) (known as the Scillitan Martyrs) – they had refused to swear an oath to the Emperor.
Nanhai inspector Kong Zhi led thousands of residents to join Liang Long's rebellion against the Han dynasty.
The volcano associated with Lake Taupō in New Zealand erupts, one of the largest on Earth in the last 5,000 years. The effects of this eruption are seen as far away as Rome and China.
Last (6th) year of Guanghe era and the start of Zhongping era of the Eastern Han dynasty.
The Yellow Turban Rebellion and Liang Province Rebellion break out in China.

Zhang Jue leads the peasant revolt against Emperor Ling of Han of the Eastern Han dynasty. Heading for the capital of Luoyang, his massive and undisciplined army (360,000 men), burns and destroys government offices and outposts.
Nobles of Britain demand that Emperor Commodus rescind all power given to Tigidius Perennis, who is eventually executed.
Zhi Yao, a Kushan Buddhist monk of Yuezhi ethnicity, translates Buddhist texts into the Chinese language during the Han dynasty.
Peasants in Gaul stage an anti-tax uprising under Maternus.
Roman governor Pertinax escapes an assassination attempt, by British usurpers.
Queen Himiko (or Shingi Waō) begins her reign in Japan (until 248).
Dong Zhuo has Liu Bian deposed, and installs Emperor Xian as emperor.
Liu Bian succeeds Emperor Ling, as Chinese emperor of the Han dynasty.
Pope Victor I succeeds Pope Eleuterus as the fourteenth pope, the first from Africa.
A part of Rome burns; Emperor Commodus orders the city to be rebuilt, under the name Colonia Commodiana.
Egypt (under Roman rule) is impoverished due to an inflation rate of 100% during the previous decade.
First year of the Chuping era of the Chinese Han Dynasty.
Battle of Jieqiao: Yuan Shao narrowly defeats Gongsun Zan, in northern China.
Lü Bu assassinates warlord Dong Zhuo, who has controlled the central government of the Han Dynasty (since 189).
Syriac Christians establish an early Christian community in Kerala, India.

In Britain, Clodius Albinus allies with Septimius Severus, and accepts the title of Caesar. British tribes take advantage of the disorder in the Empire, and damage Hadrian's Wall. Extensive repairs to the defence work is carried out by the legionaries.
Last (4th) year of Chuping era of the Chinese Han dynasty.

Septimius Severus enters the capital, and has Julianus put to death. He replaces the Praetorian Guard with a 15,000-man force from the Danubian legions, and gains control of the Roman Empire, beginning the Severan dynasty.
The Praetorian Guard assassinated Roman emperor Pertinax and sold the imperial office in an auction to Didius Julianus.
Year of the Five Emperors: Septimius Severus was proclaimed Roman emperor by his troops at Carnuntum in modern-day Austria.
Decimus Clodius Septimius Albinus Caesar becomes a Roman Consul.
First year of the Xingping era, during the Han Dynasty in China.
Emperor Septimius Severus has the Roman Senate deify the previous emperor Commodus, in an attempt to gain favor with the family of Marcus Aurelius.
In China, the Xiongnu federation crosses the Great Wall and establishes itself in Shanxi Province.
Last (2nd) year of the Xingping era during the Han Dynasty.
Emperor Septimius Severus captures and sacks Byzantium; the city is rebuilt and regains its previous prosperity.
Hadrian's Wall in Britain is partially destroyed.
In order to assure the support of the Roman legion in Germany on his march to Rome, Clodius Albinus is declared Augustus by his army while crossing Gaul.
A Christian council is held in Edessa.
Septimius Severus, who had spared the Senate at the beginning of his reign, now excludes it from controlling the Roman Empire by declaring a military dictatorship.
Yuan Shu declares himself emperor of the short-lived Zhong dynasty.
Caracalla, son of Septimius Severus, is given the title of Augustus.
Marcus I succeeds Olympianus as Patriarch of Constantinople (until 211).
Emperor Septimius Severus lays siege to the city-state Hatra in Central-Mesopotamia, but fails to capture the city despite breaching the walls.
Mesopotamia is partitioned into two Roman provinces divided by the Euphrates, Mesopotamia and Osroene.
Pope Zephyrinus succeeds Pope Victor I, as the 15th pope.
