Natalia Kills and Willy Moon were fired as judges on the second series of The X Factor New Zealand, following public backlash over comments they made to a contestant during the first live show.
Nepal was struck by a magnitude-7.8 earthquake, killing more than 8,000 people.
Passengers on a Thalys train from Amsterdam to Paris confronted and subdued an attacker who attempted a mass shooting.
Physicists of the LIGO and Virgo projects first observed gravitational waves, the existence of which was predicted by Henri Poincaré in 1905.
Russian statesman and politician Boris Nemtsov, an outspoken critic of Vladimir Putin, was assassinated in central Moscow.
Shortly after takeoff from Taipei Songshan Airport, the crew of TransAsia Airways Flight 235 shut down the wrong engine in response to a flameout, leading to a crash that resulted in 43 deaths.
Six elderly men burgled a safe-deposit facility in Hatton Garden, London, and stole items worth up to an estimated £14 million.
Suicide bombers assassinated Pakistani politician Shuja Khanzada and killed at least 21 others at his home in Attock District.
The Belgian government imposed a four-day security lockdown in Brussels based on information about potential terrorist attacks.
The JAXA space probe Akatsuki entered into orbit around Venus to study the planet's atmosphere, five years after its first attempt failed.
The Parliament of Malta moved from the Grandmaster's Palace to the purpose-built Parliament House.
The U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Obergefell v. Hodges that the right of same-sex couples to marry is guaranteed by the Fourteenth Amendment.
The co-pilot of Germanwings Flight 9525 deliberately crashed the aircraft, an Airbus A320, in a mass murder–suicide in the French Alps, killing all 150 people on board.
The ringleaders of the Bali Nine were executed in Indonesia for attempting to smuggle 8.3 kg (18 lb) of heroin to Australia in 2005.
The river cruise ship Dongfang zhi Xing capsized in the Yangtze, resulting in 442 deaths in China's worst peacetime maritime disaster.
Turkish student Özgecan Aslan was murdered during a rape attempt, sparking mass demonstrations across the country after her body was discovered two days later.

United States Environmental Protection Agency personnel accidentally caused a spillage of 3 million gallons (11 million litres) of mine waste water and tailings trapped inside the Gold King Mine near Silverton, Colorado.
Western Kentucky University announced a five-year suspension of their swimming and diving programs as a result of a hazing scandal.
A Tupolev Tu-154 of the Russian Defence Ministry crashed into the Black Sea shortly after taking off from Sochi International Airport, killing all 92 people on board.
A U.S. Army Reserve veteran ambushed and shot at police officers in Dallas, killing five of them and injuring nine others, before being killed by a bomb attached to a police robot.
A man deliberately drove a truck into crowds in Nice, France, resulting in 86 deaths.
A tram derailment in Croydon, London, killed seven people.
After gunmen took hostages the previous night at a restaurant in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, government commandos stormed the premises to bring the situation to an end.
An Islamic terrorist killed 49 people in a mass shooting at the gay nightclub Pulse in Orlando, Florida.
Andrei Karlov, Russia's ambassador to Turkey, was assassinated at an art gallery in Ankara.
Chen Quanguo became the Chinese Communist Party secretary of Xinjiang, and in that role later oversaw the creation of the Xinjiang internment camps.
Citizens of the United Kingdom voted in favour of leaving the European Union.
Flydubai Flight 981 crashed during an aborted landing at Rostov-on-Don Airport, Russia, resulting in the deaths of all 62 passengers and crew on board.
Following a number of high-profile sexual assaults, major reforms were enacted to strengthen laws related to rape in Germany.
Gunmen attacked Istanbul's Atatürk Airport, killing 45 people and injuring more than 230 others.
Harambe was shot and killed after grabbing a three-year-old boy in his enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Garden, drawing widespread criticism and inspiring internet memes.
Hillary Clinton became the first female nominee for president of the United States by a major political party at the Democratic National Convention in Philadelphia.

In the first meeting between the leaders of the Catholic Church and the Russian Orthodox Church, Pope Francis and Patriarch Kirill of Moscow signed the Havana Declaration at José Martí International Airport in Cuba.
Jo Cox, a British Member of Parliament, was murdered in her constituency.
LaMia Flight 2933 crashed near Medellín, Colombia, killing 71 people, many of whom were players from Chapecoense Football Club.
Nimr al-Nimr, a prominent Shia cleric in Saudi Arabia, was executed by the Saudi government along with 46 other people.
Park Geun-hye, the president of South Korea, was impeached, marking the culmination of the country's political scandal.
Syrian civil war: The Syrian Democratic Forces launched a successful military campaign to isolate and eventually capture Raqqa, the Islamic State's capital.
The Ecnomiohyla rabborum became extinct when the last known surviving member died in captivity.
The King of Thailand, Bhumibol Adulyadej, died after 70 years on the throne, at which point was the longest-reigning current monarch.
The Paris Agreement, an international treaty on climate change, opened for signature and was signed by 175 parties.
The Paris Agreement, under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, came into effect.
The Peace at Home Council, a faction of the Turkish Armed Forces, staged a coup d'état attempt against the government and President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan.
The evacuation of nearly 88,000 people began when a wildfire swept through Fort McMurray, Alberta, Canada, and burned for another 14 months, becoming the costliest disaster in Canadian history.
The first victims of a mass methanol poisoning which eventually killed over 70 inhabitants of Irkutsk, Russia, began arriving at hospitals.
The last nine Aston Martin DB9 units rolled off the production line, marking the end of a twelve-year manufacturing period.
The state-owned Taedonggang Brewing Company inaugurated the first beer festival in North Korea.
Thirty-six people died when a fire broke out at an illegally converted warehouse in Oakland, California, the deadliest U.S. building fire since 2003.
Two commuter trains collided head-on at Bad Aibling in southeastern Germany, killing 12 people and injuring 85.
Yemen War: A funeral in Sanaa was hit by two consecutive airstrikes by a Saudi-led coalition, leaving 143–155 civilians dead and more than 525 injured.
A Myanmar Air Force Shaanxi Y-8 crashed into the Andaman Sea near Dawei, killing all 122 people on board.
A car bomb exploded near the German embassy in Kabul, Afghanistan, killing more than 90 people and injuring 463 others.
A fire severely damaged Grenfell Tower in North Kensington, London, killing 72 people.
A hijacker deliberately drove a truck into crowds along Drottninggatan in Stockholm, Sweden, killing five people.
A homemade bomb partially exploded on an eastbound District line train at Parsons Green tube station in West London, injuring 30 passengers.
A lone gunman carried out a mass shooting at a mosque in Quebec City, Canada, killing six people and injuring up to nineteen others.
A lone gunman fired more than 1,000 rounds of ammunition from his hotel suite on a crowd attending the Route 91 Harvest music festival on the Las Vegas Strip, resulting in 60 deaths and 867 injuries.
A naming ceremony for the chemical elements moscovium, tennessine, and oganesson took place at the Russian Academy of Sciences in Moscow.
An Amtrak Cascades passenger train derailed near DuPont, Washington, killing three people and injuring sixty-five others.
An Uzbek immigrant drove a rented truck into cyclists and runners in Lower Manhattan, New York City, killing eight people.
An earthquake struck central Mexico, killing 370 people and injuring more than 6,000, exactly 32 years after the 1985 Mexico City earthquake, which killed at least 9,000 people.
Around 250,000 farmed non-native Atlantic salmon were accidentally released into the wild near Cypress Island, Washington.
British prime minister Theresa May invoked Article 50 of the Treaty on European Union, formally beginning the United Kingdom's withdrawal from the European Union.
Canadian astronomer Robert Weryk discovered ʻOumuamua, the first known interstellar object detected passing through the Solar System.
Construction began on a 69 m statue of the Buddha at Wat Paknam Bhasicharoen in Bangkok.
Cyclone Numa, a rare "medicane", made landfall in Greece to become the worst weather event that the country had experienced since 1977.
Eurovision Song Contest: Portugal won the contest for the first time, with the song "Amar pelos dois," performed by Salvador Sobral.
Hurricane Irma made landfall on Cudjoe Key, Florida, as a Category 4, after causing catastrophic damage throughout the Caribbean.
Hurricane Irma reached peak intensity near the Caribbean islands of Barbuda, Saint Martin, and Virgin Gorda.
In the U.S. state of Arizona, the Boundary Fire burned out after 32 days, burning 17,788 acres of the Coconino and Kaibab National Forests.
Kim Jong-nam, the half-brother of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, was assassinated using VX nerve agent in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.
Millions of people participated in the Women's March in Washington, D.C., and around the world to advocate for legislation and policies on human rights and other issues.
North Korea conducted its sixth and most powerful nuclear test at Punggye-ri, causing a magnitude-6.3 earthquake.
Rodrigo Duterte declared martial law in Mindanao following the Maute Group attack on Marawi.
Syrian civil war: Allied troops led by the Turkish Armed Forces captured the city of al-Bab from the Islamic State.
Syrian civil war: The Syrian Democratic Forces opened the Second Battle of Raqqa, the final phase of the Raqqa campaign, capturing the de facto capital of the Islamic State four months later.
Syrian civil war: The Syrian Democratic Forces, assisted by the U.S. military, captured the Tabqa Dam and surrounding countryside, completing the Battle of Tabqa.
The Azure Window, a limestone natural arch in Gozo, Malta, collapsed during a stor
The Louvre Abu Dhabi was inaugurated by the French president Emmanuel Macron and then-crown prince of Abu Dhabi Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan.
The Maltese journalist and anti-corruption activist Daphne Caruana Galizia was killed in a car bomb attack in Bidnija.
The Shandong was launched for the People's Liberation Army Navy, China's first domestically built aircraft carrier.
The WannaCry ransomware attack affected more than 400,000 computers worldwide, including systems used by the National Health Service and Telefónica.
The tour bus of the German football team Borussia Dortmund was attacked with roadside bombs in Dortmund, killing a police officer and injuring one of the team's players.
Turkish Airlines Flight 6491 crashed in Manas International Airport after the flight overflew the entire runway, which resulted in 39 deaths.
Two people were fatally stabbed and eight others wounded by a rejected asylum seeker in an Islamist terrorist attack in Turku, Finland.
Under President Donald Trump, the United States government officially recognized Jerusalem as the capital of Israel.
War in Afghanistan: In an airstrike in Nangarhar Province, the U.S. military dropped the most powerful conventional bomb used in combat.
Websites of Ukrainian organizations were swamped by a massive cyberattack, blamed on Russian military hackers, using the malware Petya.
Wildfires erupted across central Portugal, eventually causing the deaths of 66 people.
A bus carrying the Humboldt Broncos collided with a semi-truck, killing 16 and injuring 13.
A civilian school bus in Dahyan, Yemen, was bombed by Saudi Arabia killing at least 40 children under 15.
A civilian school bus in Dahyan, Yemen, was bombed by Saudi forces, killing at least 40 children.
A group of Taliban gunmen attacked and took hostages at the Hotel Inter-Continental Kabul, Afghanistan, sparking a 12-hour battle that left at least 21 people dead.
A magnitude-7.1 earthquake hit Anchorage, Alaska, causing 117 injuries.
A man intentionally struck pedestrians with a van on Yonge Street in Toronto, Canada, leading to 11 deaths.
A tsunami, triggered by the partial collapse of Anak Krakatoa, killed 426 people and injured over 14,000 in coastal areas of Indonesia.
A woman opened fire at YouTube headquarters in San Bruno, California, injuring three people before killing herself.
Agents with the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement raided a slaughterhouse in Tennessee, detaining nearly 100 Hispanic workers in one of the largest immigration raids in the history of the U.S.
An escalator accident in Rome left 24 people injured, mostly fans of the CSKA Moscow football team who were in town for a UEFA Champions League match against Roma.
An lone gunman shot and killed seventeen people and injured seventeen others in a mass shooting at Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School in Parkland, Florida.
Croatian Mario Mandžukić scored the first own goal in a FIFA World Cup final in their defeat to France.
Cubana de Aviación Flight 0972 crashed near Santiago de las Vegas shortly after takeoff from José Martí International Airport, killing 112 of the 113 people on board.
Emmerson Mnangagwa was elected to his first full term as president, having served as leader since the 2017 Zimbabwean coup d'état.
Following nationwide protests, Hailemariam Desalegn announced his resignation as prime minister of Ethiopia, remaining in post as a caretaker until he was succeeded by Abiy Ahmed.
For the first time since its transition to democracy, the Congress of Deputies in Spain passed a motion of no confidence against the government.
In Mrauk U, Myanmar, police fired into a crowd protesting the ban of an event to mark the anniversary of the end of the Kingdom of Mrauk U, resulting in seven deaths and twelve injuries.

In the "Minneapolis Miracle", American football player Stefon Diggs caught a 61-yard (56 m) touchdown pass that secured the Minnesota Vikings' victory in the National Football Conference divisional playoff game.
Netflix released Black Mirror: Bandersnatch, its first interactive content for adults.
Operatives of the British Special Boat Service boarded the container ship Grande Tema in the Thames Estuary to detain four stowaways who had threatened the crew.
Saratov Airlines Flight 703 crashed shortly after take-off in Russia due to icing conditions, killing all 71 people on board.
Silent Sam, a Confederate monument on the campus of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, was toppled by protestors.
The International Court of Justice ruled that Chile was under no obligation to restore Bolivia's access to the Pacific Ocean, which it had lost in the 19th century.
The Israeli Air Force conducted missile strikes that hit multiple targets in western Syria; Syrian air defences responding to the strikes accidentally downed a Russian plane.
The Japanese space probe Hayabusa2 arrived at the asteroid Ryugu to collect samples for return to Earth.
The Supreme Court of India invalidated part of Section 377 of the Penal Code, thus legalising homosexuality in India.
The Washington Post journalist Jamal Khashoggi was assassinated in the Saudi consulate in Istanbul, Turkey.
The last members of a junior association football team and their coach were rescued from Tham Luang Nang Non, a flooded cave in northern Thailand.
The wedding of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle took place at St George's Chapel in Windsor Castle, England.
Thirteen-year-old Jayme Closs was kidnapped from her home in Barron, Wisconsin, and held captive for 88 days.
A fire in an escape room in Koszalin, Poland, killed five teenagers.
A fire severely damaged Notre-Dame de Paris, destroying the cathedral's timber spire and much of the roof.
A group broke into the North Korean embassy in Madrid, Spain, and stole several mobile telephones and digital storage devices.
A major explosion at a chemical plant in Yancheng, China, killed 78 people and injured 640 others.
A mass shooting occurred at a Walmart in El Paso, Texas, killing 23 people and injuring 22 others.
A shooting at a municipal building in Virginia Beach, United States, left 13 people dead, including the gunman, and injured four others.
A sightseeing helicopter crashed in the mountains of Skoddevarre in Alta, Norway, killing all six people on board.

After being informed that its recently purchased coffin of Nedjemankh had been looted, the Metropolitan Museum of Art shuttered its ongoing exhibition Nedjemankh and His Gilded Coffin two months early and later returned the artifact to Egypt.
An arson attack at the studio of Kyoto Animation in Japan led to the deaths of 36 people.
An oil pipeline explosion killed 137 people in Tlahuelilpan, Mexico.
Anti-government protests calling for free and fair elections began in Baku, Azerbaijan.
At the Chicago Marathon, Kenyan runner Brigid Kosgei set the current marathon world record for women running in a mixed-sex race.
Boris Johnson became Prime Minister of the United Kingdom after winning the Conservative Party leadership election.
Citizenship Amendment Act protests: 10 to 15 local women blockaded a major road in Delhi, India, to protest the exclusion of Muslims from the amended Citizenship Act.
Dominican-American retired baseball player David Ortiz was shot and severely wounded while at a bar in Santo Domingo.
Drone attacks on major processing facilities at Abqaiq and Khurais forced Saudi Arabia to cut more than half of its oil production.

Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 crashed six minutes after take-off from Addis Ababa International Airport due to a fault within the software of the plane, resulting in the deaths of all 157 people on board.
Having already caused severe flooding in the Philippines, Typhoon Lekima made landfall in Zhejiang, China, killing 45 people in the province.
Iranian aircraft shot down an American drone over the Strait of Hormuz amid heightened tensions between the two countries.
Jeffrey Epstein, an American financier and convicted sex offender, was found dead in his cell at the Metropolitan Correctional Center, New York.
MBC Newsdesk reported on a nightclub assault in Seoul, South Korea, leading to the Burning Sun scandal, which involved several Korean idols and police officials.
Pakistani prime minister Imran Khan inaugurated the Kartarpur Corridor, a visa-free border crossing connecting the Gurdwara Darbar Sahib to the India–Pakistan border.
People returning from anti–extradition bill protests in Hong Kong were attacked by suspected triad members in Yuen Long, leaving 45 people injured.
President Martín Vizcarra dissolved the Congress of Peru, resulting in a constitutional crisis.
Protests in Santiago that started 11 days prior escalated into open battle against the Chilean national police, forcing President Sebastián Piñera to declare a state of emergency.
Scientists from the Event Horizon Telescope project released the first image of the black hole at the center of the galaxy M87.
Syrian civil war: The U.S. Air Force carried out an airstrike in al-Baghuz Fawqani, killing as many as 80, a disputed number of whom were civilians.
Syrian civil war: Turkish forces began an offensive into north-eastern Syria following the withdrawal of U.S. troops from the region.
The Alabama Crimson Tide and LSU Tigers football teams, both with undefeated records thus far that season, played in a "Game of the Century".
The British travel company Thomas Cook Group ceased operations with immediate effect, leaving around 600,000 tourists stranded around the world.
The Mocking of Christ by Cimabue sold at auction in France for €19.5 million, a record for a pre-1500 artwork.
The NASA space probe New Horizons flew by the trans-Neptunian object Arrokoth, making it the farthest object visited by a spacecraft.
The Supreme Court of the United Kingdom unanimously ruled that advice given by Prime Minister Boris Johnson to Queen Elizabeth II that Parliament should be prorogued was unlawful.
The United States Department of Justice released a redacted version of the Mueller report about the investigation of Russian influence on the U.S. presidential election to Congress and the public.
The inaugural race of the W Series took place at Hockenheimring, Germany, and was won by Jamie Chadwick, who later became the season's champion.

Vivianne Miedema scored six goals and had four assists for Arsenal W.F.C. in their 11–1 victory over Bristol City W.F.C., which broke the record for the most goals scored in a FA Women's Super League match.
A Sikorsky S-76 helicopter crashed in Calabasas, California, killing all nine people on board, including former basketball player Kobe Bryant and his daughter Gianna.
A landslide at a jade mine in Hpakant killed 175–200 miners, the deadliest mining accident in Burmese history.
A large explosion of ammonium nitrate stored at the Port of Beirut in Lebanon killed 218 people and caused US$15 billion in damage.
A magnitude-7.0 earthquake occurred in the Aegean Sea between Greece and Turkey, triggering a tsunami and causing 119 deaths.
A major oil spill from the Colonial Pipeline was discovered in Mecklenburg County, North Carolina.
A mid-air collision in Soldotna, Alaska, United States, killed seven people, including state representative Gary Knopp.
A series of attacks in Nova Scotia, Canada, ended when the perpetrator was killed by police, leaving 22 victims dead.
A truck struck and killed four Victoria Police officers on the Eastern Freeway, Australia, the force's deadliest single incident.
After 253 days without an operational government, a second round of investiture votes produced Spain's first coalition government since the Second Republic.
After a five day search, the body of American actress and singer Naya Rivera was recovered from Lake Piru, confirming her death.
Air India Express Flight 1344 overshot the runway at Calicut International Airport in Kerala, India, and crashed, killing 21 of the 190 people on board.
An oil spill in Norilsk released 17,500 tons of diesel oil into nearby rivers.
California wildfires: A pyrotechnic device at a gender reveal party ignited the El Dorado Fire, burning for 71 days and killing one firefighter.
Crew Dragon Demo-2 became the first commercial mission to the International Space Station.
George Floyd, a black American man, was murdered during an arrest by a white police officer in Minneapolis, sparking protests in the U.S. and other countries.
Hong Kong–based writer and publisher Gui Minhai, known for writing about Chinese Communist Party politicians, was sentenced to ten years' imprisonment for intelligence violations.
Japanese figure skater Yuzuru Hanyu won the Four Continents Championships to become the only man to complete a Super Slam.
North Macedonia became a member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO).
Nuclear physicist Mohsen Fakhrizadeh, regarded as the chief of Iran's nuclear program, was assassinated, allegedly by Mossad.
Philippine broadcast network ABS-CBN was forced to go off-air by the National Telecommunications Commission after Congress failed to renew its franchise granted in 1995.
Protests following the murder of George Floyd erupted in Minneapolis–Saint Paul before spreading across the United States and internationally.
Reddit banned r/The_Donald, a pro-Trump subreddit, for rule violations and antagonizing the company.
Second Nagorno-Karabakh War: Azerbaijani forces defeated the self-proclaimed Republic of Artsakh in the Battle of Shusha, reclaiming the town after 28 years.
Sembawang Hot Spring Park in Singapore reopened after being redeveloped by the National Parks Board.
The Abraham Accords were signed in Washington, D.C., normalizing relations between Israel and two Arab nations, the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.
The British government announced that it had removed the last land mine from the Falkland Islands, laid by Argentine forces during the 1982 Falklands War.
The El Dorado Fire in California, United States, was extinguished after 71 days, having destroyed 20 structures and killed one firefighter.
The World Health Organization (WHO) declared the COVID-19 virus epidemic a pandemic.
The World Health Organization (WHO) officialy declared the COVID-19 outbreak as a pandemic.
The World Health Organization declared the COVID-19 pandemic to be a public health emergency of international concern.
A cable car crashed, killing 14 people near Lake Maggiore in northern Italy.
A container ship ran aground and obstructed the Suez Canal for six days.
A crowd crush killed 45 people during the annual pilgrimage to the tomb of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in Israel.
A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck in Haiti, killing at least 2,248 people and causing $1.5 billion in damages and economic loss.
A man rammed a pickup truck into Muslim Pakistani Canadian pedestrians in Ontario, Canada, killing four members of the same family.
A mass shooting at a FedEx Ground facility in Indianapolis, Indiana, killed nine and injured seven.
A portion of a 12-story condominium building collapsed in Surfside, Florida, United States, killing 98 people and injuring 11 others.
A series of four explosions at a military barracks in Bata, Equatorial Guinea caused at least 107 deaths.
A tornado strikes an Amazon warehouse during increased holiday demand, killing six sheltering workers.
An elevated section of the Mexico City Metro collapsed, killing 26 people and injuring 98 others.

At the season-ending Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, Max Verstappen overtook Lewis Hamilton on the final lap to become World Drivers' Champion.
Burmese military forces killed at least 40 civilians during the Mo So massacre in Kayah State, Myanmar.
Bus drivers in Greater Manchester began an eleven-week strike, one of the longest in British transportation history.
Derek Chauvin was found guilty of all charges in the murder of George Floyd by a Minnesota court.
Head of a Bear sold at auction in London for a total of £8.8 million, a record for a drawing by Leonardo da Vinci.
Myanmar civil war: Burmese military and police forces killed at least 82 civilians in the Bago massacre, including people protesting a recent coup d'état.
Prince Philip, the consort of Queen Elizabeth II, died at Windsor Castle aged 99.
Riots in four Ecuadorian prisons, caused by gang rivalries, resulted in the deaths of 79 inmates.
Ryanair Flight 4978 was forced to land by Belarusian authorities, who detained dissident journalist Roman Protasevich.
Six people, including the perpetrator, were killed in a mass shooting in Plymouth, England.

Supporters of then-outgoing U.S. president Donald Trump attack the United States Capitol to disrupt certification of the 2020 presidential election, resulting in five deaths and evacuation of the U.S. Congress.

The Indonesian Navy submarine Nanggala imploded and sank in the Bali Sea, resulting in the deaths of all 53 people on board.
The second phase of the Thomson-East Coast MRT line was opened for service.

After losing a league home match to their local rivals, Persebaya Surabaya, around 3,000 Arema supporters invaded the pitch at Kanjuruhan Stadium, prompting police to fire tear gas and causing a stampede that killed 135.
American climate activist Wynn Bruce set himself on fire outside the United States Supreme Court Building in an apparent protest against the climate crisis.
An 18-year old gunman shot and killed nineteen students and two teachers in a mass shooting at Robb Elementary School in Uvalde, Texas.
An earthquake registering 6.2 Mw caused the deaths of at least 1,000 people in Afghanistan and Pakistan.
At 49 days, Liz Truss concluded the shortest tenure as prime minister of the United Kingdom.
At the 94th Academy Awards, Will Smith slapped Chris Rock onstage resulting in Smith being expelled from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and banned from its events for ten years.
Former Japanese prime minister Shinzo Abe was assassinated with an improvised firearm.
Members of the European Parliament, including Vice President Eva Kaili, and their associates are arrested in connection with the Qatar corruption scandal.
Myanmar civil war: Burmese military forces launched airstrikes that killed at least 80 concertgoers in Kachin State.
Myanmar civil war: Government troops killed 37 unarmed civilians in Mondaingbin.
Pakistani journalist Arshad Sharif is shot and killed by local police in Kajiado, Kenya.
Palestinian-American journalist Shireen Abu Akleh was shot and killed while reporting on an Israel Defense Forces raid on the Jenin refugee camp.
Protests broke out across Chad after President Mahamat Déby declared his intentions to extend his rule by another two years.
Queen Elizabeth II died at Balmoral Castle in Scotland; her eldest son Charles III acceded to the throne as King of the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth realms.
Russian forces captured the city of Kherson, the only regional capital to be taken during the Russian invasion of Ukraine.
Russian invasion of Ukraine: Russian forces captured the city of Sievierodonetsk, Ukraine, after six weeks of fighting.
Russo-Ukrainian war: Russia claimed full control of Mariupol after a nearly three-month siege.
The Duffield Memorial in Great Baddow, an "unusual example of Art Nouveau design in metal work", was designated a listed building by Historic England.
The Event Horizon Telescope released the first image of Sagittarius A*.
A Myanmar Air Force airstrike killed at least 100 villagers in Pazigyi.
A collision between two passenger trains and a parked freight train near the city of Balasore, Odisha, in eastern India resulted in 296 deaths and more than 1,200 people injured.
A freight train derailed in East Palestine, Ohio, releasing hazardous materials into the surrounding area.
A series of mass protests began in Belgrade, Serbia, alleging electoral irregularities in the Serbian parliament and Belgrade city assembly elections.
A shooting at a dance studio in Monterey Park, California, left 11 people dead and injured nine others.

A tourist boat capsized, killing at least 22 people in Tanur, India.
Chinese authorities cancelled a run of performances of The Mongol Khan, the first Mongolian play to be performed internationally, forty minutes before its planned premiere in Hohhot.
Donald Trump became the first former U.S. president to be indicted by a grand jury.
Ecuadorian presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio was assassinated in Quito, eleven days before the general election.
Forty people are killed in a fire at a migrant detention facility in Ciudad Juárez, Mexico.
Fox News agreed to pay Dominion Voting Systems a $787 million settlement over defamation claims related to the 2020 U.S. presidential election.
Hibiscus Rising, a sculpture commemorating the life of David Oluwale, was unveiled in Leeds.

Irish broadcaster RTÉ announced that between 2017 and 2022 it had paid €345,000 more than had been previously disclosed to presenter Ryan Tubridy.
King Charles III and Queen Camilla were crowned at Westminster Abbey in London.
Pakistani protests: Riots broke out following the arrest of former Pakistani prime minister Imran Khan.
SpaceX's Starship launched for the first time before exploding four minutes into flight.
The Sycamore Gap tree in Northumberland, England, was illegally felled.
The Titan submersible imploded during a dive to the RMS Titanic wreck, killing all five people aboard.
The World Health Organization declared the end of COVID-19 as a global health emergency.
A plane crash in Malawi, kills nine people, including Vice President Saulos Chilima.
Acting president and prime minister of South Korea Han Duck-soo was impeached by the National Assembly.

After the loss of aircraft systems, Azerbaijan Airlines Flight 8243 crashed near Aktau International Airport while attempting to perform an emergency landing after being hit by a Russian defense missile.
At least 145 people were killed and 551 injured in a bombing and mass shooting at the Crocus City Hall in Krasnogorsk, Russia.
Donald Trump was convicted of falsifying business records in a New York trial, becoming the first former U.S. president found guilty in a criminal case.
Flooding in the Persian Gulf began, killing 19 in Oman.
In Iran, a helicopter crash killed eight people, including President Ebrahim Raisi and Foreign Minister Hossein Amir-Abdollahian.
Jeju Air Flight 2216 crashed at Muan International Airport while attempting to perform a belly-landing after losing engine thrust to a flock of Baikal teal.
Keir Starmer led the Labour Party to a landslide victory in the United Kingdom general election, ending fourteen years of Conservative rule.
Neary's, a New York City Irish pub popular with political elites, closed.
Prabowo Subianto and Gibran Rakabuming Raka were sworn in as president and vice president of Indonesia, becoming the oldest and the youngest person to assume respective offices.
Prime Minister of Slovakia Robert Fico is hospitalised after an assassination attempt.
Several thousand North Korean migrant workers in Helong engaged in civil unrest, including a factory occupation and the taking of managers as hostages, due to unpaid wages.
South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol declares martial law.
The Francis Scott Key Bridge collapsed following a collision between the MV Dali container ship and one of the bridge's support pillars, killing 6 people.
The Greenfield tornado, estimated to have produced winds in excess of 309 mph, moved across Iowa.
The Syrian civil war ended when Bashar al-Assad's party, the Syrian Ba'ath Party, surrendered to the Syrian opposition.
Urfan Sharif and Beinash Batool were found guilty of the murder of Sara Sharif, and were sentenced to life imprisonment.
Voepass Linhas Aéreas Flight 2283 crashed near Vinhedo, São Paulo, Brazil, killing all 62 people on board.
While landing at Haneda Airport, Japan Airlines Flight 516 collided with a De Havilland Canada Dash 8 which killed five people in total.
A UPS Airlines plane crashed in Louisville, Kentucky, killing at least twelve people.
A car rammed into a crowd on Water Street, Liverpool, injuring 65 people.
A crowd crush outside M. Chinnaswamy Stadium during celebrations of Royal Challengers Bengaluru's Indian Premier League title killed 11 people and injured 56 others.
A fire at a hotel at the Kartalkaya ski resort in Turkey's Bolu Province results in 78 people killed.
A magnitude-7.7 earthquake killed more than 5,000 people in Myanmar and Thailand.
Air India Flight 171 crashed shortly after take-off in Ahmedabad, India, killing 260 people.
American political activist Charlie Kirk was shot and killed at an event at Utah Valley University.
Filmmakers Rob Reiner and Michele Singer Reiner are stabbed to death in their Brentwood, Los Angeles residence.
Former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years in prison for his involvement in a coup plot.
Gaza war: Israel Defense Forces killed 15 aid workers in the Rafah paramedic massacre.
Israel recognises Somaliland as an independent state, becoming the first country to do so.
Prime minister of Mongolia Luvsannamsrain Oyun-Erdene resigned after weeks of protests.
Ukrainian politician Andriy Parubiy was assassinated in Lviv, Ukraine.
A gas explosion at a coal mine in Changzhi, Shanxi, China, leaves at least 82 people dead.
A suicide bombing targeting a shuttle train in Quetta, Balochistan, Pakistan, kills at least 47 people.
An avalanche on Broad Peak in Pakistan kills 10 climbers.
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor became the first member of the British royal family to be arrested in 379 years.
During the Artemis II mission, the Orion made its closest approach to the far side of the Moon and reached its greatest distance from Earth.
Malian minister of defence Sadio Camara is killed during the start of coordinated attacks in the country.
The United States and Israel launched strikes against Iran, killing Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and other senior officials.
The United States launches a military operation in Venezuela, capturing president Nicolás Maduro and his wife.
